---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m3p4t0 ----------------------------
(* A small fleet of warehouse robots shares one loading bay of bounded    *)
(* capacity CAP.  A leader is elected among the robots and only the live  *)
(* (non-crashed) leader may grant a robot entry to the bay.  The leader   *)
(* can crash silently (it stops responding but its identity is still     *)
(* recorded as "leader" until a surviving robot notices and fails over). *)
(* The invariant below guards that the bay never holds more robots than  *)
(* CAP allows, regardless of how leadership churns during failover.      *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS ROBOTS, CAP

VARIABLES leader, epoch, crashed, inBay

vars == <<leader, epoch, crashed, inBay>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in ROBOTS
  /\ epoch \in Nat
  /\ crashed \subseteq ROBOTS
  /\ inBay \subseteq ROBOTS

Init ==
  /\ leader \in ROBOTS
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ inBay = {}

\* The twist: exactly one robot may ever crash silently, and only if it
\* is currently the leader (a crashed follower has no effect on leadership).
LeaderCrash ==
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ crashed' = {leader}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, inBay>>

\* Failover: once the leader has silently crashed, some other live robot
\* takes over leadership and a new epoch begins.
Failover(r) ==
  /\ leader \in crashed
  /\ r \notin crashed
  /\ r # leader
  /\ leader' = r
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, inBay>>

\* Only a live (non-crashed) leader may admit a robot into the bay, and
\* only while the bay has spare capacity.
Enter(r) ==
  /\ leader \notin crashed
  /\ r \notin crashed
  /\ r \notin inBay
  /\ Cardinality(inBay) < CAP
  /\ inBay' = inBay \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, crashed>>

Leave(r) ==
  /\ r \in inBay
  /\ inBay' = inBay \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, crashed>>

Next ==
  \/ LeaderCrash
  \/ \E r \in ROBOTS : Failover(r) \/ Enter(r) \/ Leave(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* PROPERTY: the loading bay never holds more robots than its bounded
\* capacity, even across leader crash and failover.
CapacityOK == Cardinality(inBay) <= CAP

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  ROBOTS = {r1, r2, r3}
  CAP = 2
INVARIANT CapacityOK
nl:
A small fleet of warehouse robots (drawn from the set ROBOTS) shares a single loading bay with a bounded capacity CAP. Only one robot at a time can be the fleet's elected leader, and only the currently live leader is trusted to grant a robot permission to enter the bay -- this keeps the physical bay from ever being overloaded even though many robots may want to load or unload at once.

The fleet uses leader election with failover to stay operational: a leader is chosen at startup, and if it ever goes silent -- crashing without sending any warning, rather than announcing a graceful handoff -- the surviving robots eventually notice and promote one of themselves to be the new leader, bumping an epoch counter so stale leadership claims can be told apart from the current one. Because the crash is silent, the system has no dedicated "crash detected" step; the crashed leader simply stops being able to satisfy the "live leader" guard that entry requires, and any robot may then step up to become the new leader via failover.

The full action set is:
- LeaderCrash: the current leader silently crashes. This can happen to at most one robot ever, and only while it is the leader -- it does not send any signal, it just becomes unable to satisfy the live-leader guard from then on.
- Failover(r): once the leader has crashed, some other still-live robot r takes over as leader and the epoch counter increases, marking the new term.
- Enter(r): a robot r that is not crashed enters the loading bay, but only if the current leader is still live (not crashed) and the bay is not already at its capacity CAP.
- Leave(r): a robot r currently in the bay leaves it, freeing up a slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of robots simultaneously occupying the loading bay never exceeds the fleet's bounded capacity CAP, regardless of how leadership changes hands during a silent crash and failover.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m8p2t3 ---------------------------
(* A blood-bank inventory tracker moves units between blood-type bins     *)
(* under a hierarchical locking protocol: a worker first grabs the       *)
(* coarse, bank-wide lock, then the finer per-transfer lock, before it   *)
(* is allowed to actually move a unit from one bin to another.  The      *)
(* worker carrying out the move may be slow (it can take many "Work"     *)
(* steps before finishing) but it never fails outright, so the transfer  *)
(* always eventually completes and the lock is always eventually freed. *)
(* The safety invariant guards that units are only ever moved between    *)
(* bins, never created or destroyed; the liveness property guarantees    *)
(* the hierarchical lock is always eventually released again.           *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS TYPES, START, BUSYMAX

VARIABLES phase, pending, inv, busy

vars == <<phase, pending, inv, busy>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in {"Idle", "CoarseHeld", "FineHeld"}
  /\ pending \in TYPES \X TYPES
  /\ inv \in [TYPES -> Nat]
  /\ busy \in 0..BUSYMAX

Init ==
  /\ phase = "Idle"
  /\ pending \in TYPES \X TYPES
  /\ inv = [t \in TYPES |-> START]
  /\ busy = 0

\* Step 1 of the hierarchical lock: grab the coarse, bank-wide lock and
\* declare which two bins the pending transfer will touch.
AcquireCoarse(src, dst) ==
  /\ phase = "Idle"
  /\ src # dst
  /\ inv[src] > 0
  /\ phase' = "CoarseHeld"
  /\ pending' = <<src, dst>>
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inv, busy>>

\* Step 2 of the hierarchical lock: once the coarse lock is held, acquire
\* the fine-grained lock on the specific pair of bins and start the
\* (possibly slow) physical unit move.
AcquireFine ==
  /\ phase = "CoarseHeld"
  /\ phase' = "FineHeld"
  /\ busy' = BUSYMAX
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, inv>>

\* The twist: the worker holding the fine lock may be slow -- it can take
\* many steps to physically carry the unit across -- but it is never
\* failed, so busy always keeps counting down towards zero.
Work ==
  /\ phase = "FineHeld"
  /\ busy > 0
  /\ busy' = busy - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, pending, inv>>

\* Once the slow move finishes, the unit is debited from the source bin
\* and credited to the destination bin in one atomic step, and both
\* locks (fine, then implicitly coarse) are released together.
CompleteTransfer ==
  /\ phase = "FineHeld"
  /\ busy = 0
  /\ inv' = [inv EXCEPT ![pending[1]] = @ - 1, ![pending[2]] = @ + 1]
  /\ phase' = "Idle"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, busy>>

Next ==
  \/ AcquireFine
  \/ Work
  \/ CompleteTransfer
  \/ \E src, dst \in TYPES : AcquireCoarse(src, dst)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(AcquireFine)
  /\ WF_vars(Work)
  /\ WF_vars(CompleteTransfer)

\* SAFETY: no unit is ever created or destroyed -- the total across all
\* bins always equals the total the bank started with.
RECURSIVE SumInv(_)
SumInv(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET t == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
       IN inv[t] + SumInv(S \ {t})

TotalUnits == SumInv(TYPES)
InitialTotal == Cardinality(TYPES) * START

Conservation == TotalUnits = InitialTotal

\* LIVENESS: the hierarchical lock (coarse held, then fine held) is
\* always eventually released again -- the tracker keeps returning to Idle.
AlwaysEventuallyIdle == []<>(phase = "Idle")

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  TYPES = {bt1, bt2, bt3}
  START = 2
  BUSYMAX = 2
INVARIANT Conservation
PROPERTY AlwaysEventuallyIdle
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker keeps count of blood units held in a small number of type-specific bins (drawn from the set TYPES). To move a unit from one bin to another -- for example when components are re-pooled or relabeled between compatible types -- a worker must go through a hierarchical locking protocol: it first acquires a coarse, bank-wide lock that reserves the bank for a single pending transfer, and only after that may it acquire the finer per-transfer lock on the specific pair of bins involved. Only once both locks are held does the worker actually touch the inventory counts.

The twist is that the worker carrying out the physical move can be slow: instead of moving the unit in a single step, it may need an arbitrary but bounded number of "still working" steps before the transfer finishes. Crucially the worker is never considered failed -- it always keeps making progress and the countdown always reaches zero -- so the coarse-then-fine lock it holds is guaranteed to eventually be released, it just might take a while. This models a real bank where a technician double-checks labels and paperwork before finalizing a transfer, rather than a machine that can crash mid-transfer.

The full action set is:
- AcquireCoarse(src, dst): while the tracker is idle, a worker reserves the bank-wide coarse lock for a transfer moving a unit from bin src to bin dst (src and dst must differ, and src must currently hold at least one unit).
- AcquireFine: once the coarse lock is held, the worker acquires the fine-grained lock on the specific (src, dst) pair and begins the physical move, starting a countdown of work steps.
- Work: while the fine lock is held and the countdown has not reached zero, the slow worker takes one more step of progress, decrementing the countdown -- it never fails, so this always eventually reaches zero.
- CompleteTransfer: once the countdown reaches zero, the worker debits one unit from src and credits one unit to dst in a single atomic step, then releases both the fine and coarse locks, returning the tracker to idle.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of blood units summed across all bins never changes -- units are only ever moved between bins by the locking protocol, never created or destroyed.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a transfer has acquired the hierarchical lock, the tracker always eventually returns to the idle state, i.e. the coarse-then-fine lock is always eventually released again even though the worker holding it may be slow.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m9p6t4 ----------------------------
(* An elevator bank uses epoch-numbered reconfiguration to change its    *)
(* runtime capacity (how many cars may be simultaneously dispatched).    *)
(* Every reconfiguration bumps a global epoch number and immediately     *)
(* recalls every dispatched car, since a car that has not yet resynced   *)
(* to the new epoch is no longer authorized to be serving a floor call   *)
(* under the old configuration.  The invariant below guards that only    *)
(* cars whose locally-known epoch matches the bank's current epoch are   *)
(* ever found active -- a stale car can never be caught mid-dispatch.    *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS CARS, MAXCAP, EPOCHMAX

VARIABLES epoch, cap, carEpoch, active

vars == <<epoch, cap, carEpoch, active>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..EPOCHMAX
  /\ cap \in 1..MAXCAP
  /\ carEpoch \in [CARS -> 0..EPOCHMAX]
  /\ active \subseteq CARS

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ cap = MAXCAP
  /\ carEpoch = [c \in CARS |-> 0]
  /\ active = {}

\* The twist: bank capacity can change at runtime.  Doing so bumps the
\* epoch and immediately recalls every currently-active car, because no
\* car can yet have resynced to an epoch that was just minted.
Reconfigure(newCap) ==
  /\ epoch < EPOCHMAX
  /\ newCap \in 1..MAXCAP
  /\ newCap # cap
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ cap' = newCap
  /\ active' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED carEpoch

\* A car resynchronizes its locally-known epoch to the bank's current
\* one, becoming authorized to accept dispatches again.
Sync(c) ==
  /\ carEpoch[c] # epoch
  /\ carEpoch' = [carEpoch EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap, active>>

\* Only a car whose epoch matches the bank's current epoch may be
\* dispatched, and only while the (possibly just-changed) capacity has
\* a free slot.
Dispatch(c) ==
  /\ carEpoch[c] = epoch
  /\ c \notin active
  /\ Cardinality(active) < cap
  /\ active' = active \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap, carEpoch>>

Release(c) ==
  /\ c \in active
  /\ active' = active \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap, carEpoch>>

Next ==
  \/ \E newCap \in 1..MAXCAP : Reconfigure(newCap)
  \/ \E c \in CARS : Sync(c)
  \/ \E c \in CARS : Dispatch(c)
  \/ \E c \in CARS : Release(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: every car currently active (serving a floor call) must be
\* running under the bank's current epoch -- an unauthorized or stale
\* car (one still carrying an old epoch) is never found active.
NoStaleAction == \A c \in active : carEpoch[c] = epoch

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  CARS = {c1, c2, c3}
  MAXCAP = 3
  EPOCHMAX = 3
INVARIANT NoStaleAction
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper manages a fleet of cars (drawn from the set CARS) using epoch-numbered reconfiguration. The bank maintains a global epoch number and a current capacity -- the maximum number of cars that may be simultaneously dispatched to serve floor calls. Each car locally remembers the last epoch it has synced to. A car is only authorized to be dispatched, or to remain dispatched, while its locally-known epoch matches the bank's current epoch; a car still carrying an older epoch number is considered stale and must resync before it can act again.

The twist is that the bank's capacity can change at runtime -- for instance to take a car offline for maintenance, or to bring more cars online during a rush -- and every such capacity change is implemented as a reconfiguration that mints a brand-new epoch. Because no car can have possibly resynced to an epoch that was just minted, a reconfiguration immediately recalls every car that was active under the old configuration: they must resync to the new epoch before being dispatched again. This prevents any car from continuing to act under stale, superseded authorization once the bank's configuration has moved on.

The full action set is:
- Reconfigure(newCap): the bank controller changes its capacity to newCap (a different value than the current one), bumping the epoch number and immediately recalling every currently active car.
- Sync(c): car c whose locally-known epoch does not match the bank's current epoch resynchronizes to the current epoch, becoming authorized again.
- Dispatch(c): the controller dispatches car c to serve a floor call, but only if c's locally-known epoch matches the bank's current epoch (c is not stale) and the current capacity has a free slot.
- Release(c): an active car c finishes serving its call and becomes idle again, freeing a capacity slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A car is never found dispatched (active) while carrying an epoch number that differs from the bank's current epoch -- no unauthorized or stale car can ever be caught acting.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m5p4t5 ----------------------------
(* A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker admits new players by quorum      *)
(* voting: an existing member proposes a candidate, current members cast *)
(* votes, and the candidate is admitted once a strict majority of the    *)
(* current membership approves.  A privileged admin can bypass the vote  *)
(* entirely to force an add, but even the admin can never push the lobby *)
(* past its bounded capacity.  The safety invariant guards that bound;   *)
(* the liveness property guarantees that every opened vote is eventually *)
(* resolved (either the candidate is admitted or the proposal lapses),   *)
(* so the matchmaker never gets stuck mid-vote.                          *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS PLAYERS, CAP

VARIABLES members, votes, pending, phase

vars == <<members, votes, pending, phase>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ members \subseteq PLAYERS
  /\ votes \subseteq PLAYERS
  /\ pending \in PLAYERS \cup {"none"}
  /\ phase \in {"Idle", "Voting"}

Init ==
  /\ members = {}
  /\ votes = {}
  /\ pending = "none"
  /\ phase = "Idle"

\* Open a vote on admitting candidate p, but only while the lobby has a
\* free slot -- an already-full lobby cannot even start a proposal.
ProposeJoin(p) ==
  /\ phase = "Idle"
  /\ p \notin members
  /\ Cardinality(members) < CAP
  /\ phase' = "Voting"
  /\ pending' = p
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED members

\* An existing member casts an approval vote for the pending candidate.
Vote(m) ==
  /\ phase = "Voting"
  /\ m \in members
  /\ m \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<members, pending, phase>>

\* Once a strict majority of the current membership has approved, the
\* candidate is admitted -- the capacity guard is rechecked defensively.
CommitJoin ==
  /\ phase = "Voting"
  /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes) > Cardinality(members)
  /\ Cardinality(members) < CAP
  /\ members' = members \cup {pending}
  /\ phase' = "Idle"
  /\ pending' = "none"
  /\ votes' = {}

\* If every current member has already voted and a majority still was
\* not reached, the proposal cannot possibly succeed and lapses.
AbandonProposal ==
  /\ phase = "Voting"
  /\ members \ votes = {}
  /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes) <= Cardinality(members)
  /\ phase' = "Idle"
  /\ pending' = "none"
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED members

\* The twist: a privileged admin can force-add a player without any
\* vote at all, but is still bound by the same capacity limit as
\* every ordinary quorum-approved join.
AdminForceAdd(p) ==
  /\ phase = "Idle"
  /\ p \notin members
  /\ Cardinality(members) < CAP
  /\ members' = members \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, pending, phase>>

Leave(m) ==
  /\ m \in members
  /\ members' = members \ {m}
  /\ votes' = votes \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, phase>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in PLAYERS : ProposeJoin(p)
  \/ \E m \in PLAYERS : Vote(m)
  \/ CommitJoin
  \/ AbandonProposal
  \/ \E p \in PLAYERS : AdminForceAdd(p)
  \/ \E m \in PLAYERS : Leave(m)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A m \in PLAYERS : WF_vars(Vote(m))
  /\ WF_vars(CommitJoin)
  /\ WF_vars(AbandonProposal)

\* SAFETY: the lobby never holds more players than its bounded capacity,
\* whether they arrived through a quorum-approved vote or an admin
\* override.
CapacityOK == Cardinality(members) <= CAP

\* LIVENESS: every proposal that opens a vote is eventually resolved --
\* the matchmaker never stalls forever in the middle of a vote.
VotingResolves == (phase = "Voting") ~> (phase = "Idle")

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  PLAYERS = {p1, p2, p3, p4}
  CAP = 3
INVARIANT CapacityOK
PROPERTY VotingResolves
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker admits players (drawn from the set PLAYERS) into a shared lobby of bounded capacity CAP using quorum voting: to add a new player, an existing lobby member opens a proposal naming a candidate, and current members cast approval votes on that candidate. The candidate is only admitted once a strict majority of the current membership has voted yes -- ordinary joins always go through this collective, quorum-gated process.

The twist is that there is a privileged admin who can force-add a player to the lobby without going through any vote at all -- useful for seeding a match quickly or resolving a stuck lobby -- but the admin's override never lets the lobby exceed its bounded capacity: the same capacity check that gates a quorum-approved join also gates the admin's forced add. If every current member has already cast a vote and a majority still was not reached, the proposal is abandoned rather than left open forever, so the matchmaker is guaranteed to keep making progress.

The full action set is:
- ProposeJoin(p): while no vote is in progress and the lobby has a free slot, a member opens a vote proposing to admit candidate p.
- Vote(m): an existing member m who has not yet voted on the open proposal casts an approval vote.
- CommitJoin: once a strict majority of current members has voted yes (and the lobby still has a free slot), the pending candidate is admitted and the vote closes.
- AbandonProposal: once every current member has voted and a majority was not reached, the open proposal lapses and the vote closes without admitting anyone.
- AdminForceAdd(p): the privileged admin adds candidate p directly, bypassing the vote entirely, but only while the lobby has a free slot under the same capacity bound.
- Leave(m): an existing member m leaves the lobby, freeing a slot and withdrawing any vote it had cast.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The lobby never holds more players than its bounded capacity CAP, regardless of whether players arrive through a quorum-approved vote or the admin's override.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every proposal that opens a vote is eventually resolved -- the matchmaker always eventually returns to the idle state rather than stalling forever in the middle of a vote.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m1p2t0 ----------------------------
(* A university course-registration system arranges its registrar nodes  *)
(* in a token ring: only whichever node currently holds the token may    *)
(* move a seat between the shared seat pool and a student's enrollment   *)
(* count.  The ring is resilient to a single silently-crashed node --    *)
(* the token-forwarding mechanism simply routes around it, the way a     *)
(* real token-ring LAN regenerates a lost token after a timeout.  The    *)
(* invariant below guards that seats are only ever moved between the     *)
(* pool and enrollment counts, never created or destroyed, no matter how *)
(* the token circulates or which single node has silently gone dark.     *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS n1, n2, n3, TOTAL

NODES == {n1, n2, n3}
RING == <<n1, n2, n3>>

VARIABLES token, crashed, pool, enrolled

vars == <<token, crashed, pool, enrolled>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in NODES
  /\ crashed \subseteq NODES
  /\ pool \in 0..TOTAL
  /\ enrolled \in [NODES -> 0..TOTAL]

Init ==
  /\ token \in NODES
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ pool = TOTAL
  /\ enrolled = [n \in NODES |-> 0]

\* Ring-order successor of n, found by looking n up in the fixed ring
\* sequence RING and wrapping around.
Idx(n) == CHOOSE i \in 1..Len(RING) : RING[i] = n
Succ(n) == RING[(Idx(n) % Len(RING)) + 1]

\* The token skips at most one silently-crashed node when it is passed --
\* this is the ring's built-in resilience to the twist.
NextAlive(n) ==
  LET s == Succ(n)
  IN IF s \notin crashed THEN s ELSE Succ(s)

\* The twist: exactly one registrar node may ever go silently dark; a
\* crashed node can no longer register or drop students, but the ring
\* still forwards the token around it.
CrashSilently ==
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ \E n \in NODES : crashed' = {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, pool, enrolled>>

\* The ring forwards the token to the next live node, timing out and
\* bypassing a silently-crashed holder if necessary.
PassToken ==
  /\ token' = NextAlive(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, pool, enrolled>>

\* Only the current, live token holder may move a seat out of the shared
\* pool into its own enrollment count.
Register(n) ==
  /\ token = n
  /\ n \notin crashed
  /\ pool > 0
  /\ pool' = pool - 1
  /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![n] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, crashed>>

\* Only the current, live token holder may return one of its enrolled
\* seats back to the shared pool.
Drop(n) ==
  /\ token = n
  /\ n \notin crashed
  /\ enrolled[n] > 0
  /\ pool' = pool + 1
  /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![n] = @ - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, crashed>>

Next ==
  \/ CrashSilently
  \/ PassToken
  \/ \E n \in NODES : Register(n) \/ Drop(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: the total number of seats -- those still in the shared pool
\* plus those currently enrolled anywhere -- always equals TOTAL. No
\* seat is ever created or destroyed by token circulation or crashes.
RECURSIVE SumEnrolled(_)
SumEnrolled(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET n == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
       IN enrolled[n] + SumEnrolled(S \ {n})

Conservation == pool + SumEnrolled(NODES) = TOTAL

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  n1 = n1
  n2 = n2
  n3 = n3
  TOTAL = 3
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
A university course-registration system spreads its work across a handful of registrar nodes (drawn from the set NODES) arranged in a fixed token ring. There is a single shared pool of seats for a course, and only whichever node currently holds the token is allowed to move a seat between the shared pool and its own count of enrolled students. This gives each node exclusive, non-overlapping access to modify the seat counts, one node at a time, as the token circulates around the ring.

The twist is that exactly one registrar node can crash silently at any point -- it simply stops responding, with no warning or graceful shutdown. Once a node has crashed it can no longer register or drop students itself, but the ring's token-forwarding mechanism is resilient to this: when the token would be passed to a crashed node, the ring times out and forwards it on to the next live node instead, the way a real token-ring network regenerates a lost token after a silence. This keeps registration moving even with one dead node in the ring.

The full action set is:
- CrashSilently: one registrar node (at most one, ever) goes silently dark and can no longer register or drop students.
- PassToken: the ring forwards the token to the next node in ring order, automatically skipping over a silently-crashed node if necessary.
- Register(n): the node n that currently holds the token, provided it has not crashed, moves one seat out of the shared pool into its own enrolled-student count.
- Drop(n): the node n that currently holds the token, provided it has not crashed, returns one of its enrolled seats back to the shared pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of seats -- summing the shared pool and every node's enrolled count -- always equals the course's fixed total capacity; no seat is ever created or destroyed as the token circulates or a single node silently crashes.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m2p3t0 ---------------------------
(* A blood-bank inventory tracker allocates storage slots to requesters  *)
(* using two-phase commit across its participant branches: a slot's     *)
(* transaction first enters a Preparing phase where every live branch   *)
(* votes yes, and only once all live branches have voted does the       *)
(* coordinator commit the allocation.  One branch can crash silently    *)
(* mid-vote; rather than blocking the slot forever, the coordinator      *)
(* eventually aborts a transaction that is waiting on a crashed voter.   *)
(* The safety invariant guards that a slot is never committed to two     *)
(* different requesters; the liveness property guarantees every         *)
(* Preparing transaction eventually reaches a decision (commit or        *)
(* abort), even in the presence of the silent crash.                    *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS SLOTS, PARTICIPANTS

VARIABLES phase, votes, txOwner, committed, crashed

vars == <<phase, votes, txOwner, committed, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in [SLOTS -> {"Idle", "Preparing"}]
  /\ votes \in [SLOTS -> SUBSET PARTICIPANTS]
  /\ txOwner \in [SLOTS -> PARTICIPANTS \cup {"none"}]
  /\ committed \subseteq (SLOTS \X PARTICIPANTS)
  /\ crashed \subseteq PARTICIPANTS

Init ==
  /\ phase = [s \in SLOTS |-> "Idle"]
  /\ votes = [s \in SLOTS |-> {}]
  /\ txOwner = [s \in SLOTS |-> "none"]
  /\ committed = {}
  /\ crashed = {}

\* Only a currently-free slot (no existing commit record) may start a
\* new allocation transaction, moving it into the Preparing phase.
StartAlloc(s, p) ==
  /\ phase[s] = "Idle"
  /\ ~ \E q \in PARTICIPANTS : <<s, q>> \in committed
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![s] = "Preparing"]
  /\ txOwner' = [txOwner EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, crashed>>

\* A live (non-crashed) branch casts its yes vote for the pending
\* transaction on slot s.
VoteYes(s, q) ==
  /\ phase[s] = "Preparing"
  /\ q \notin crashed
  /\ q \notin votes[s]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = @ \cup {q}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, txOwner, committed, crashed>>

\* Once every currently-live branch has voted yes, and the slot is still
\* free, the coordinator commits the allocation to the requester.
Commit(s) ==
  /\ phase[s] = "Preparing"
  /\ (PARTICIPANTS \ crashed) \subseteq votes[s]
  /\ ~ \E q \in PARTICIPANTS : <<s, q>> \in committed
  /\ committed' = committed \cup {<<s, txOwner[s]>>}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![s] = "Idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, txOwner, crashed>>

\* The twist: if a crashed branch is still being waited on for its vote
\* on slot s, the coordinator times out and aborts rather than blocking
\* the slot forever.
AbortOnCrash(s) ==
  /\ phase[s] = "Preparing"
  /\ \E q \in crashed : q \notin votes[s]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![s] = "Idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, txOwner, committed, crashed>>

\* At most one participant branch may ever go silently dark.
CrashSilently ==
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ \E q \in PARTICIPANTS : crashed' = {q}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, txOwner, committed>>

\* Once a committed slot's blood unit has been used, the slot is
\* recycled back to the free pool so it can be allocated again later.
Release(s) ==
  /\ \E q \in PARTICIPANTS : <<s, q>> \in committed
  /\ LET owner == CHOOSE p \in PARTICIPANTS : <<s, p>> \in committed
     IN committed' = committed \ {<<s, owner>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, txOwner, crashed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in SLOTS, p \in PARTICIPANTS : StartAlloc(s, p)
  \/ \E s \in SLOTS, q \in PARTICIPANTS : VoteYes(s, q)
  \/ \E s \in SLOTS : Commit(s)
  \/ \E s \in SLOTS : AbortOnCrash(s)
  \/ CrashSilently
  \/ \E s \in SLOTS : Release(s)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A s \in SLOTS, q \in PARTICIPANTS : WF_vars(VoteYes(s, q))
  /\ \A s \in SLOTS : WF_vars(Commit(s))
  /\ \A s \in SLOTS : WF_vars(AbortOnCrash(s))

\* SAFETY: a slot is never committed to two different requesters -- if
\* two commit records exist for the same slot, they name the same owner.
NoDoubleAlloc ==
  \A s \in SLOTS :
    \A p, q \in PARTICIPANTS :
      (<<s, p>> \in committed /\ <<s, q>> \in committed) => p = q

\* LIVENESS: every transaction that enters the Preparing phase for a
\* slot eventually reaches a decision -- either commit or the
\* crash-triggered abort -- so no slot is ever stuck Preparing forever.
AllocDecided ==
  \A s \in SLOTS : (phase[s] = "Preparing") ~> (phase[s] = "Idle")

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker allocates a small number of storage slots (drawn from SLOTS) to requesters using two-phase commit across its participant branches (drawn from PARTICIPANTS). To allocate a currently free slot, a transaction enters a Preparing phase naming the requesting owner, and every live branch must cast a yes vote before the coordinator will commit the allocation. Only once every currently-live branch has voted, and the slot is still free, does the coordinator finalize the commit record for that slot.

The twist is that exactly one participant branch can crash silently at any point -- it simply stops responding and will never cast another vote. Rather than letting this permanently block a slot whose transaction is waiting on that branch's vote, the coordinator eventually times out: if a crashed branch is still being awaited for a given slot's transaction, the coordinator aborts that transaction and returns the slot to the idle, unallocated state so a fresh attempt can be made later. This means a single silent crash can never wedge a slot's allocation forever.

The full action set is:
- StartAlloc(s, p): while slot s is idle and has no existing commit record, a transaction begins, proposing to allocate s to requester p and entering the Preparing phase.
- VoteYes(s, q): a live (non-crashed) branch q that has not yet voted on slot s's pending transaction casts its yes vote.
- Commit(s): once every currently-live branch has voted yes on slot s's transaction, and the slot is still free, the coordinator commits the allocation to the requester and the slot returns to idle.
- AbortOnCrash(s): if a crashed branch is still being waited on for slot s's transaction, the coordinator aborts the transaction (rather than blocking forever) and the slot returns to idle, unallocated.
- CrashSilently: at most one participant branch, ever, goes silently dark and stops voting from then on.
- Release(s): once slot s's committed blood unit has been used, the slot is recycled back to the free pool, clearing its commit record so it can be allocated again later.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A slot is never committed to two different requesters -- whenever two commit records exist for the same slot, they always name the same owner, so no slot is ever double-allocated.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every transaction that enters the Preparing phase for a slot eventually reaches a decision -- either it commits or the crash-triggered timeout aborts it -- so no slot is ever left stuck in Preparing forever, even with one branch silently crashed.

(* A university course-registration system protects its shared           *)
(* registration ledger -- the critical resource where seat counts are    *)
(* actually written -- with a token ring: a node may only enter the      *)
(* critical section while it both holds the ring token and has an open   *)
(* request to write.  The ring tolerates a single silently-crashed node  *)
(* by forwarding the token past it once the section is clear.  The       *)
(* invariant below is the mutual-exclusion guarantee: it is never the    *)
(* case that two different nodes are simultaneously inside the critical  *)
(* section, no matter how requests queue up or a node silently dies.     *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS n1, n2, n3

NODES == {n1, n2, n3}

\* Fixed ring order, defined directly as a successor function rather
\* than via an index into a sequence.
NEXT ==
  [x \in NODES |->
    CASE x = n1 -> n2
      [] x = n2 -> n3
      [] x = n3 -> n1]

VARIABLES holder, inCS, crashed, requesting

vars == <<holder, inCS, crashed, requesting>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ holder \in NODES
  /\ inCS \subseteq NODES
  /\ crashed \subseteq NODES
  /\ requesting \subseteq NODES

Init ==
  /\ holder \in NODES
  /\ inCS = {}
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ requesting = {}

\* The ring bypasses a silently-crashed node when forwarding the token,
\* but only once the critical section is empty.
NextAlive(x) ==
  LET s == NEXT[x]
  IN IF s \notin crashed THEN s ELSE NEXT[s]

\* The twist: exactly one node may ever go silently dark; once crashed
\* it can no longer request or enter the critical section.
CrashSilently ==
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ \E n \in NODES : crashed' = {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, inCS, requesting>>

\* A live node signals that it wants to write to the shared ledger.
Request(n) ==
  /\ n \notin crashed
  /\ n \notin requesting
  /\ requesting' = requesting \cup {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, inCS, crashed>>

\* The ring forwards the token to the next live node, but only while the
\* critical section is clear -- the token cannot move mid-write.
PassToken ==
  /\ inCS = {}
  /\ holder' = NextAlive(holder)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, crashed, requesting>>

\* Only the live node currently holding the token, and which has an
\* outstanding request, may enter the critical section.
EnterCS(n) ==
  /\ n = holder
  /\ n \notin crashed
  /\ n \in requesting
  /\ n \notin inCS
  /\ inCS' = inCS \cup {n}
  /\ requesting' = requesting \ {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed>>

ExitCS(n) ==
  /\ n \in inCS
  /\ inCS' = inCS \ {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed, requesting>>

Next ==
  \/ CrashSilently
  \/ PassToken
  \/ \E n \in NODES : Request(n) \/ EnterCS(n) \/ ExitCS(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: mutual exclusion of the shared ledger -- no two distinct
\* nodes are ever simultaneously inside the critical section, whether
\* because of request ordering, token circulation, or a silent crash.
MutualExclusion == \A n, m \in inCS : n = m

A university course-registration system protects its shared registration ledger -- the single critical resource where seat and enrollment changes are actually committed -- using a token ring among its registrar nodes (drawn from the set NODES). A node may only write to the ledger (enter the critical section) while it both currently holds the ring's token and has an outstanding request to do so. Nodes must first request access, then wait for the token to reach them, before they may enter.

The twist is that exactly one node can crash silently at any point -- it stops responding entirely, with no warning. A crashed node can no longer request access or enter the critical section, but the ring's token-forwarding mechanism is resilient to this single failure: the token is only ever passed while the critical section is empty, and when it would be passed to a crashed node, the ring instead forwards it on to the next live node in ring order. - EnterCS(n): the live node n that currently holds the token, and has an outstanding request, enters the critical section.
- ExitCS(n): a node n currently inside the critical section leaves it, clearing the way for the token to move again.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m7p1t5 ---------------------------
(* A subway signalling block system guards entry to each track block     *)
(* with a compare-and-swap register: a train that wants to occupy a      *)
(* block reads the block's current version, then only actually claims    *)
(* the block if the version has not moved since its read.  If another    *)
(* train (or the signalling admin) has changed the block in the          *)
(* meantime, the CAS is rejected and the train must re-read and retry,   *)
(* or abandon the attempt if the block is now genuinely occupied by      *)
(* someone else -- it never silently believes it grabbed the block when  *)
(* it did not.  The safety invariant guards against exactly that lost    *)
(* update; the liveness property guarantees every claim attempt is       *)
(* eventually resolved, even with a bounded number of emergency admin    *)
(* overrides interleaved.                                                *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS TRAINS, BLOCKS, VERMAX, MAXOVERRIDE

VARIABLES ver, occ, attempting, seenVer, overridesUsed

vars == <<ver, occ, attempting, seenVer, overridesUsed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ ver \in [BLOCKS -> 0..VERMAX]
  /\ occ \in [BLOCKS -> TRAINS \cup {"empty"}]
  /\ attempting \in [TRAINS -> BLOCKS \cup {"none"}]
  /\ seenVer \in [TRAINS -> 0..VERMAX]
  /\ overridesUsed \in 0..MAXOVERRIDE

Init ==
  /\ ver = [b \in BLOCKS |-> 0]
  /\ occ = [b \in BLOCKS |-> "empty"]
  /\ attempting = [t \in TRAINS |-> "none"]
  /\ seenVer = [t \in TRAINS |-> 0]
  /\ overridesUsed = 0

\* A free train reads a currently-empty block's version and begins a
\* claim attempt against that snapshot.
StartClaim(t, b) ==
  /\ attempting[t] = "none"
  /\ occ[b] = "empty"
  /\ attempting' = [attempting EXCEPT ![t] = b]
  /\ seenVer' = [seenVer EXCEPT ![t] = ver[b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, occ, overridesUsed>>

\* The compare-and-swap succeeds only if the block's version is still
\* exactly what the train saw, and the block is still empty -- this is
\* what prevents a lost update: the train can only ever believe it won
\* the block if nothing else changed it out from under it.
CasSucceed(t) ==
  LET b == attempting[t] IN
    /\ attempting[t] # "none"
    /\ ver[b] = seenVer[t]
    /\ occ[b] = "empty"
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = t]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = (ver[b] + 1) % (VERMAX + 1)]
    /\ attempting' = [attempting EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seenVer, overridesUsed>>

\* The block is still empty but its version moved since the train's
\* snapshot (someone else claimed and released it, or the admin
\* cleared it) -- the train refreshes its snapshot and will retry.
CasRetry(t) ==
  LET b == attempting[t] IN
    /\ attempting[t] # "none"
    /\ ver[b] # seenVer[t]
    /\ occ[b] = "empty"
    /\ seenVer' = [seenVer EXCEPT ![t] = ver[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, occ, attempting, overridesUsed>>

\* The block turns out to be genuinely occupied by someone else -- the
\* train gives up rather than retrying forever against a taken block.
AbandonClaim(t) ==
  LET b == attempting[t] IN
    /\ attempting[t] # "none"
    /\ occ[b] # "empty"
    /\ occ[b] # t
    /\ attempting' = [attempting EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, occ, seenVer, overridesUsed>>

Release(t, b) ==
  /\ occ[b] = t
  /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = "empty"]
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = (ver[b] + 1) % (VERMAX + 1)]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<attempting, seenVer, overridesUsed>>

\* The twist: a privileged signalling-center admin can force-clear an
\* occupied block directly, bypassing the compare-and-swap check
\* entirely -- but only a bounded number of times across the run.
AdminOverride(b) ==
  /\ overridesUsed < MAXOVERRIDE
  /\ occ[b] # "empty"
  /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = "empty"]
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = (ver[b] + 1) % (VERMAX + 1)]
  /\ overridesUsed' = overridesUsed + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<attempting, seenVer>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in TRAINS, b \in BLOCKS : StartClaim(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in TRAINS : CasSucceed(t)
  \/ \E t \in TRAINS : CasRetry(t)
  \/ \E t \in TRAINS : AbandonClaim(t)
  \/ \E t \in TRAINS, b \in BLOCKS : Release(t, b)
  \/ \E b \in BLOCKS : AdminOverride(b)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A t \in TRAINS : SF_vars(CasSucceed(t))
  /\ \A t \in TRAINS : SF_vars(CasRetry(t))
  /\ \A t \in TRAINS : SF_vars(AbandonClaim(t))

\* SAFETY: no lost update -- a train is never simultaneously recorded
\* as the occupant of a block and still marked as attempting to claim
\* that same block. A successful compare-and-swap always atomically
\* clears the in-flight attempt in the very step that grants ownership,
\* so a train can never lose track of, or blindly retry over, its own
\* just-committed write.
NoLostUpdate ==
  \A t \in TRAINS :
    \A b \in BLOCKS :
      (occ[b] = t) => (attempting[t] # b)

\* LIVENESS: every claim attempt a train starts is eventually resolved
\* -- either the compare-and-swap succeeds or the train abandons once
\* it sees the block is genuinely taken -- despite contention and the
\* admin's bounded emergency overrides.
ClaimResolves ==
  \A t \in TRAINS : (attempting[t] # "none") ~> (attempting[t] = "none")

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS

  BLOCKS = {b1, b2}
  VERMAX = 2
  MAXOVERRIDE = 1
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate

nl:
A subway signalling block system guards entry to each track block (drawn from BLOCKS) with a compare-and-swap register: the register holds a version number and the identity of whichever train (if any) currently occupies the block. A train (drawn from TRAINS) that wants to occupy an empty block first reads the block's current version, then attempts to swap itself in -- but the swap only succeeds if the version has not changed since the train's read. If another train's swap, a release, or the admin's override has moved the version in the meantime, the compare-and-swap is rejected: the train must re-read the block's latest version and retry, or if the block turns out to be genuinely occupied by someone else, abandon the attempt rather than retrying forever against a taken block. This is exactly what protects against a lost update: a train can never end up believing it silently overwrote or acquired a block that someone else actually holds.

The twist is that a privileged signalling-center admin can force-clear an occupied block directly, bypassing the compare-and-swap check entirely -- useful for an emergency stop or manual reset -- but this override capability is only available a bounded number of times across the scenario, since it is meant for rare emergency use rather than routine operation.

The full action set is:
- StartClaim(t, b): a free train t (not currently attempting anything) that finds block b empty reads its current version and begins a claim attempt against that snapshot.
- CasSucceed(t): the compare-and-swap succeeds for train t's in-progress attempt because the block's version still matches what t read and the block is still empty; t becomes the occupant and the version advances.
- CasRetry(t): the block t is attempting is still empty but its version has moved since t's snapshot; t refreshes its snapshot and will try again.
- AbandonClaim(t): the block t is attempting turns out to be occupied by a different train; t gives up the attempt rather than retrying against a block that is genuinely taken.
- Release(t, b): the train t currently occupying block b releases it, returning the block to empty and advancing its version.
- AdminOverride(b): the privileged admin force-clears an occupied block b directly, without any compare-and-swap check, advancing its version -- but only while the bounded override budget has not yet been used up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No lost updates -- a train is never simultaneously recorded as the occupant of a block while still marked as attempting to claim that same block, since a successful compare-and-swap always atomically clears the in-flight attempt in the same step that grants ownership.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every claim attempt a train starts is eventually resolved -- either the compare-and-swap succeeds or the train abandons once the block is genuinely taken by someone else -- despite contention among trains and the admin's bounded emergency overrides.

---- MODULE W4Od14m3p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* A wildfire-surveillance drone swarm holds a fixed pool of TotalZones patrol
\* zones. Zones are bookkept as a count per drone (assigned), and leadership
\* moves between drones as they crash and recover (failover). Zones held by a
\* crashed drone can only be reclaimed by the current leader (FailoverClaim),
\* except that AdminId is a privileged drone that may reassign zone-counts
\* directly between any two currently-alive drones (AdminOverride), bypassing
\* the normal leader-only failover path. The Conservation invariant checks
\* that no zone-count is ever created or destroyed across all of this churn.

CONSTANTS Drones, AdminId, TotalZones, MaxTerm
NoLeader == "NoLeader"

VARIABLES alive, leader, assigned, term

vars == <<alive, leader, assigned, term>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ alive \subseteq Drones
  /\ leader \in Drones \cup {NoLeader}
  /\ assigned \in [Drones -> 0..TotalZones]
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm

Init ==
  /\ alive = Drones
  /\ leader = AdminId
  /\ assigned = [d \in Drones |-> IF d = AdminId THEN TotalZones ELSE 0]
  /\ term = 0

\* A drone drops off the network without warning (silent crash).
Crash(d) ==
  /\ d \in alive
  /\ alive' = alive \ {d}
  /\ leader' = IF leader = d THEN NoLeader ELSE leader
  /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, term>>

\* Any surviving drone may step up when there is no leader.
Elect(d) ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ d \in alive
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ leader' = d
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, assigned>>

\* The current leader reclaims the zone-count still recorded against a
\* crashed drone, folding it into its own count.
FailoverClaim(d, f) ==
  /\ leader = d
  /\ f \in Drones \ alive
  /\ assigned[f] > 0
  /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![f] = 0, ![d] = @ + assigned[f]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, leader, term>>

\* Privileged override: the admin drone, if alive, may move zone-count
\* directly between any two alive drones, regardless of who is leader.
AdminOverride(src, dst, amt) ==
  /\ AdminId \in alive
  /\ src \in alive /\ dst \in alive /\ src # dst
  /\ amt \in 1..assigned[src]
  /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![src] = @ - amt, ![dst] = @ + amt]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, leader, term>>

\* A crashed drone rejoins the swarm, still owning whatever zone-count it
\* held at crash time.
Recover(d) ==
  /\ d \in Drones \ alive
  /\ alive' = alive \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, assigned, term>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Drones : Crash(d)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : Elect(d)
  \/ \E d, f \in Drones : FailoverClaim(d, f)
  \/ \E src, dst \in Drones, amt \in 1..TotalZones : AdminOverride(src, dst, amt)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : Recover(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
       IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

\* The swarm's total patrol-zone count is neither created nor destroyed by
\* crashes, failover reclaims, admin overrides, or recoveries.
Conservation == SumOver(assigned, Drones) = TotalZones

CONSTANTS
  Drones = {d1, d2, d3}
  AdminId = d1
  TotalZones = 4
  MaxTerm = 3
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
A wildfire surveillance drone swarm patrols a fixed set of forest zones. The
swarm elects one drone as leader through a lightweight leader-election
protocol with failover: whenever there is no leader, any surviving drone may
step forward and claim the role. Each drone in the swarm keeps a bookkept
count of how many patrol zones it is currently responsible for, and the
total number of zones across the whole swarm is fixed by design — zones are
never invented out of thin air and never quietly vanish, only handed off
between drones as leadership changes hands.

Drones can drop off the mesh network without warning (a silent crash caused
by battery failure, a downed relay, or a wildfire itself damaging hardware).
When a drone crashes, its zone-count stays recorded against it until the
current leader performs a failover reclaim, folding the crashed drone's
zone-count into its own tally. Crashed drones can also rejoin the swarm
later, at which point they still own whatever zone-count they held at the
moment they went dark. Sitting above the normal election-and-failover path
is one privileged admin drone, which — whenever it is alive — may directly
reassign zone-count between any two currently-alive drones, bypassing the
requirement that only the leader may perform reassignment. This override
exists so a human operator can rebalance the swarm during an emergency
without waiting for a new election.

The full action set is: Crash (a drone silently drops off the network,
losing leadership if it held it), Elect (a surviving drone claims
leadership when none is set), FailoverClaim (the leader reclaims the
zone-count still recorded against a crashed drone), AdminOverride (the
privileged admin drone moves zone-count directly between any two alive
drones, bypassing the leader-only path), and Recover (a crashed drone
rejoins the swarm, retaining its previously recorded zone-count).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the sum of the zone-counts
recorded across all drones in the swarm equals the swarm's fixed total
number of patrol zones — no zone-count is ever created or destroyed by
crashes, elections, failover reclaims, or admin overrides.

---- MODULE W4Od18m7p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* A smart-home door lock network shares a pool of unlock tokens guarded by a
\* compare-and-swap (CAS) register `reg`. A lock wanting to unlock reads the
\* register (Request), then attempts a CAS (AcquireCAS) that only succeeds if
\* the register is unchanged since the read; otherwise the CAS fails
\* (FailCAS) and the lock must re-read and retry. Held tokens are returned to
\* the pool on Release. The home's total token capacity is not fixed forever:
\* an admin action may raise or lower it at runtime (Increase/DecreaseCapacity)
\* as locks are added to or retired from the network. Conservation checks
\* that free tokens plus held tokens always exactly equal current capacity --
\* no token is ever invented or lost by the CAS retry loop itself.

CONSTANTS Locks, MinCap, MaxCap, InitCap

VARIABLES reg, state, snapshot, capacity

vars == <<reg, state, snapshot, capacity>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in 0..MaxCap
  /\ state \in [Locks -> {"idle", "reading", "holding"}]
  /\ snapshot \in [Locks -> 0..MaxCap]
  /\ capacity \in MinCap..MaxCap

Init ==
  /\ reg = InitCap
  /\ state = [l \in Locks |-> "idle"]
  /\ snapshot = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
  /\ capacity = InitCap

\* A lock about to request unlock reads the current register value.
Request(l) ==
  /\ state[l] = "idle"
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![l] = "reading"]
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![l] = reg]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, capacity>>

\* CAS succeeds: the register still matches what was read, and a token
\* is available, so the lock atomically takes it.
AcquireCAS(l) ==
  /\ state[l] = "reading"
  /\ snapshot[l] = reg
  /\ reg > 0
  /\ reg' = reg - 1
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![l] = "holding"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snapshot, capacity>>

\* CAS fails: the register moved since the read (another lock or the
\* admin changed it), so the lock discards its stale read and retries.
FailCAS(l) ==
  /\ state[l] = "reading"
  /\ snapshot[l] # reg
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![l] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, snapshot, capacity>>

\* A held token is returned to the shared pool.
Release(l) ==
  /\ state[l] = "holding"
  /\ reg' = reg + 1
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![l] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snapshot, capacity>>

\* Admin adds capacity at runtime (e.g. a new relay comes online): both
\* the ceiling and the free pool grow by the same amount.
IncreaseCapacity(amt) ==
  /\ amt \in 1..(MaxCap - capacity)
  /\ capacity' = capacity + amt
  /\ reg' = reg + amt
  /\ UNCHANGED <<state, snapshot>>

\* Admin retires capacity at runtime; only free (unheld) tokens can be
\* withdrawn, never a token a lock is actively holding.
DecreaseCapacity(amt) ==
  /\ amt \in 1..(capacity - MinCap)
  /\ reg >= amt
  /\ capacity' = capacity - amt
  /\ reg' = reg - amt
  /\ UNCHANGED <<state, snapshot>>

Next ==
  \/ \E l \in Locks : Request(l)
  \/ \E l \in Locks : AcquireCAS(l)
  \/ \E l \in Locks : FailCAS(l)
  \/ \E l \in Locks : Release(l)
  \/ \E amt \in 1..MaxCap : IncreaseCapacity(amt)
  \/ \E amt \in 1..MaxCap : DecreaseCapacity(amt)

\* Every lock that manages to acquire a token must eventually give it back;
\* nothing about the CAS retry loop or capacity churn may strand a token.
Fairness == \A l \in Locks : WF_vars(Release(l))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* Free tokens plus tokens currently held always equal current capacity.
Conservation == reg + Cardinality({l \in Locks : state[l] = "holding"}) = capacity

\* Liveness: a lock holding a token does not hold it forever.
EventualRelease == \A l \in Locks : (state[l] = "holding") ~> (state[l] = "idle")

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Locks = {l1, l2}
  MinCap = 1
  MaxCap = 3
  InitCap = 2
INVARIANT Conservation
PROPERTY EventualRelease
nl:
A smart-home door lock network shares a small pool of unlock tokens guarded
by a compare-and-swap (CAS) register. Any lock that wants to unlock must
first read the register's current value, then attempt an atomic
compare-and-swap: the swap only succeeds if the register still holds the
exact value the lock read and at least one token remains free. If some
other lock (or the admin) changed the register in between, the CAS fails
and the lock discards its stale read and must re-read and retry. Once a
lock has acquired a token, it eventually releases it back to the shared
pool.

The network's total token capacity is not fixed for the lifetime of the
home: an administrator can raise or lower it at runtime as locks are
physically added to or retired from the network (a new relay coming online
increases capacity, and decommissioning an old lock decreases it). Raising
capacity mints new free tokens into the pool; lowering capacity withdraws
free tokens from the pool, but only tokens nobody is currently holding --
capacity can never be shrunk out from under a lock that is mid-unlock. At
every point, the number of free tokens plus the number of tokens currently
held by locks must exactly equal the network's current capacity: nothing
in the CAS retry loop, the release path, or the capacity-change mechanism
may invent or lose a token.

The full action set is: Request (a lock reads the register's current
value before attempting a swap), AcquireCAS (the register still matches
the lock's stale-free read and a token is free, so the swap succeeds and
the lock takes the token), FailCAS (the register moved since the read, so
the swap fails and the lock returns to idle to retry), Release (a lock
returns its held token to the shared pool), IncreaseCapacity (the admin
raises the network's capacity and mints the corresponding free tokens),
and DecreaseCapacity (the admin lowers the network's capacity by
withdrawing an equal number of currently-free tokens).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of free tokens in
the register plus the number of tokens currently held by locks equals the
network's current capacity exactly.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every lock that acquires an unlock token via a
successful CAS eventually releases it back to the shared pool.

---- MODULE W4Od18m7p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers

\* A smart-home door lock network keeps one shared record (e.g. the access
\* schedule byte a lock enforces) guarded by a compare-and-swap register.
\* Each household member caches a local snapshot (version, value) from a
\* Read, computes an intended new value (ProposeWrite), and only commits it
\* if the record's version has not moved since their snapshot (CommitWrite);
\* otherwise their attempt is stale and must be abandoned (AbortWrite) so
\* they can re-read. A privileged admin action (AdminOverride) may write the
\* record directly without holding a matching snapshot at all -- but it must
\* still bump the version, so it cannot silently masquerade as the version a
\* stale user already believes is current. NoLostUpdates checks that a
\* member's cached snapshot is never simultaneously "fresh" (version match)
\* and wrong -- the CAS discipline never lets a write based on stale data
\* land undetected.

CONSTANTS Users, MaxVal, MaxVersion

VARIABLES version, value, local, pending

vars == <<version, value, local, pending>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
  /\ value \in 0..MaxVal
  /\ local \in [Users -> [ver: 0..MaxVersion, val: 0..MaxVal]]
  /\ pending \in [Users -> (-1)..MaxVal]

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ value = 0
  /\ local = [u \in Users |-> [ver |-> 0, val |-> 0]]
  /\ pending = [u \in Users |-> -1]

\* A member refreshes their cached snapshot of the shared record.
Read(u) ==
  /\ pending[u] = -1
  /\ local' = [local EXCEPT ![u] = [ver |-> version, val |-> value]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, value, pending>>

\* A member computes an intended new value locally, based on their cache,
\* without touching the shared record yet.
ProposeWrite(u, newVal) ==
  /\ pending[u] = -1
  /\ newVal \in 0..MaxVal
  /\ newVal # local[u].val
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![u] = newVal]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, value, local>>

\* CAS commit: only succeeds if the member's cached version still matches
\* the record's current version -- i.e. nobody committed since their Read.
CommitWrite(u) ==
  /\ pending[u] # -1
  /\ local[u].ver = version
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ value' = pending[u]
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![u] = -1]
  /\ UNCHANGED local

\* A member abandons a pending write -- typically because their cache has
\* gone stale (the usual CAS-retry trigger), but this is always available
\* whenever a write is pending. That matters once the version counter
\* reaches its ceiling: it guarantees the household is never stuck holding
\* a pending write that can no longer legally be committed.
AbortWrite(u) ==
  /\ pending[u] # -1
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![u] = -1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, value, local>>

\* Privileged admin override: writes the record directly, without holding
\* any matching CAS snapshot, but still advances the version so that any
\* member's outstanding stale snapshot is provably no longer current.
AdminOverride(newVal) ==
  /\ newVal \in 0..MaxVal
  /\ newVal # value
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ value' = newVal
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<local, pending>>

Next ==
  \/ \E u \in Users : Read(u)
  \/ \E u \in Users, newVal \in 0..MaxVal : ProposeWrite(u, newVal)
  \/ \E u \in Users : CommitWrite(u)
  \/ \E u \in Users : AbortWrite(u)
  \/ \E newVal \in 0..MaxVal : AdminOverride(newVal)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: whenever a member's cached version looks current, its
\* cached value must actually be the record's current value -- a write can
\* never be silently overwritten out from under a snapshot that is still
\* considered fresh.
NoLostUpdates == \A u \in Users : (local[u].ver = version) => (local[u].val = value)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Users = {u1, u2}
  MaxVal = 2
  MaxVersion = 3
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
nl:
A smart-home door lock network keeps one shared record -- the access
schedule byte that governs when the front door will accept a code -- and
guards it with a compare-and-swap register instead of a lock. Any household
member who wants to change the schedule must first read the record's
current version and value into a local cache, then compute the new value
they want to write. When they attempt to commit, the write only succeeds if
the record's version has not moved since their read: if some other member
(or the admin) committed a change in the meantime, the commit is rejected
as stale and the member must discard their attempt and read the record
again before retrying. This optimistic-concurrency discipline is exactly
what stops two members' concurrent edits from silently clobbering one
another -- a "no lost updates" guarantee.

Sitting above this peer-to-peer CAS discipline is one privileged admin
action: the household administrator may write the record directly at any
time, without needing to hold a matching cached snapshot the way ordinary
members do. This override still advances the record's version counter,
though, so it can never be confused with -- or silently absorbed into -- a
version any member's stale cache still thinks is current; any member with
an in-flight commit attempt based on an now-outdated snapshot will still
have that commit correctly rejected next time they try.

The full action set is: Read (a member refreshes their local cache with
the record's current version and value), ProposeWrite (a member computes
an intended new value locally, based on their cache, without touching the
shared record yet), CommitWrite (a compare-and-swap commit that only
succeeds if the member's cached version still matches the record's current
version), AbortWrite (a member abandons a pending write -- typically
because their cache has gone stale, but this is always available whenever
a write is pending, so nobody is ever stuck holding a write that can no
longer be committed), and AdminOverride (the privileged admin writes the
record directly, bypassing the CAS check entirely, while still advancing
the version).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a household member's locally cached version
equals the shared record's current version, that member's cached value
must equal the record's current value -- no committed write to the shared
record is ever lost or silently overwritten out from under a snapshot that
still looks fresh.

---- MODULE W4Od3m4p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

\* A bank's interbank settlement batch runs one shared ledger that only one
\* participant may write to at a time. Participants submit settlement jobs
\* into a bounded work queue (Submit is refused once the queue is full --
\* backpressure). The settlement engine dequeues FIFO and grants exclusive
\* ledger access (Acquire); the holder either finishes normally (Release,
\* after which it is free to submit its next job) or -- the twist -- exactly
\* one designated participant, CrashProne, may crash silently while holding
\* the ledger (CrashWhileHolding) or while merely queued (CrashQueued). A
\* watchdog eventually reclaims the ledger from a crashed holder
\* (WatchdogRelease) so the batch is never wedged forever by the one
\* participant that can go dark. ExclusiveAccess checks that at most one
\* participant ever holds the ledger at once, crash or no crash.

CONSTANTS Banks, Cap, CrashProne

VARIABLES queue, holders, crashed, done

vars == <<queue, holders, crashed, done>>

NotQueued(b) == ~ (\E i \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[i] = b)

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq(Banks)
  /\ Len(queue) <= Cap
  /\ holders \subseteq Banks
  /\ crashed \subseteq Banks
  /\ done \subseteq Banks

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ holders = {}
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ done = {}

\* A participant submits a settlement job; backpressure rejects it once the
\* bounded queue is full. A bank may resubmit again after finishing a
\* previous job -- the batch runs continuously, not just once per bank.
Submit(b) ==
  /\ b \notin crashed
  /\ holders # {b}
  /\ NotQueued(b)
  /\ Len(queue) < Cap
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, b)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, crashed, done>>

\* The engine grants exclusive ledger access to the participant at the head
\* of the queue, but only when nobody currently holds it.
Acquire ==
  /\ holders = {}
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ holders' = {Head(queue)}
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, done>>

\* The holder finishes its settlement normally and releases the ledger.
Release(b) ==
  /\ holders = {b}
  /\ b \notin crashed
  /\ holders' = {}
  /\ done' = done \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, crashed>>

\* Twist: the one crash-prone participant may crash silently while still
\* holding the ledger -- it does not release it itself.
CrashWhileHolding ==
  /\ holders = {CrashProne}
  /\ CrashProne \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {CrashProne}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, holders, done>>

\* A watchdog reclaims the ledger from a holder that is known to have
\* crashed, so a silent crash cannot wedge the batch forever. The crashed
\* participant's job is never marked done -- it was only reclaimed.
WatchdogRelease(b) ==
  /\ holders = {b}
  /\ b \in crashed
  /\ holders' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, crashed, done>>

\* The crash-prone participant can also crash while merely queued (not yet
\* holding the ledger); its pending job simply drops out of the queue.
CrashQueued ==
  /\ CrashProne \notin crashed
  /\ \E i \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[i] = CrashProne
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {CrashProne}
  /\ queue' = SelectSeq(queue, LAMBDA x : x # CrashProne)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, done>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Banks : Submit(b)
  \/ Acquire
  \/ \E b \in Banks : Release(b)
  \/ CrashWhileHolding
  \/ \E b \in Banks : WatchdogRelease(b)
  \/ CrashQueued

\* Whatever wedged the lock, it is always possible to eventually free it
\* again -- either the holder finishes, or the watchdog reclaims it.
ReleaseStep(b) == Release(b) \/ WatchdogRelease(b)

Fairness ==
  /\ WF_vars(Acquire)
  /\ \A b \in Banks : WF_vars(ReleaseStep(b))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* Mutual exclusion: at most one participant ever holds the shared ledger.
ExclusiveAccess == Cardinality(holders) <= 1

\* Liveness: a participant that acquires the ledger does not keep it
\* forever -- either it finishes normally or the watchdog reclaims it after
\* the one crash-prone participant silently goes dark.
EventualRelease == \A b \in Banks : (holders = {b}) ~> (holders = {})

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Banks = {b1, b2, b3}
  Cap = 2
  CrashProne = b1
INVARIANT ExclusiveAccess
PROPERTY EventualRelease
nl:
A bank runs an interbank settlement batch against a single shared ledger.
Only one participant bank may hold write access to the ledger at a time, so
settlement jobs are staged through a bounded work queue: a bank submits a
job, and the settlement engine dequeues jobs FIFO, granting exclusive
ledger access to one bank at a time. When the queue is already full, new
submissions are refused outright -- backpressure that keeps the batch from
being flooded faster than it can be settled. The batch runs continuously:
once a bank finishes a settlement it is free to submit another job later.

The twist is that exactly one designated participant in the batch is known
to be crash-prone, and it can go dark silently at any point, including in
the middle of holding exclusive ledger access. A crash never announces
itself: the participant simply stops responding. If the crash-prone
participant crashes while it is still queued (not yet holding the ledger),
its pending job is simply dropped from the queue. If it crashes while it
actually holds the ledger, though, it does not release the lock itself --
without some recovery mechanism the batch would wedge forever with the
ledger held by a participant that will never call back in. A watchdog
process detects this and forcibly reclaims the ledger from the
known-crashed holder, though its settlement is never marked as having
completed -- it was only reclaimed, not finished. Every other participant
in the batch is reliable and never crashes.

The full action set is: Submit (a bank submits a settlement job into the
bounded queue, refused once the queue is full), Acquire (the engine grants
exclusive ledger access to the bank at the head of the queue, only when
nobody currently holds it), Release (the current holder finishes its
settlement normally and gives up the ledger, free to submit again later),
CrashWhileHolding (the crash-prone participant crashes silently without
releasing the ledger it holds), WatchdogRelease (the watchdog reclaims the
ledger from a holder that has crashed, without marking its job done), and
CrashQueued (the crash-prone participant crashes silently while merely
queued, and its pending job is dropped).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, at most one participant bank
holds exclusive access to the shared settlement ledger at a time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: A bank that acquires exclusive access to the ledger
does not hold it forever -- it is eventually released, either because the
bank finishes normally or because the watchdog reclaims it after the
crash-prone participant silently goes dark.

---- MODULE W4Od18m8p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, TLC

\* A smart-home door lock network uses hierarchical locking: a controller
\* must hold a coarse zone lock before it may hold any fine-grained door
\* lock inside that zone. Requests travel as pending messages in two
\* unordered sets (msgsZone, msgsDoor) rather than a queue, so the manager
\* may grant ANY pending request next -- messages can be reordered in
\* transit, and a door-acquire request can even be delivered and considered
\* before its matching zone-acquire request. Safety survives this only
\* because GrantDoor re-checks the CURRENT zone-lock ownership at grant
\* time rather than trusting message order. HierarchicalMutex checks that
\* whenever a door is held, its zone is held by that same controller.

\* Controllers, zones and doors are bound as individual model values (not
\* an opaque constant set) so the fixed door-to-zone topology can be
\* defined right here in the module -- TLC's .cfg constant syntax cannot
\* itself express a function-valued CONSTANT.
CONSTANTS c1, c2, z1, z2, d1, d2
NoOwner == "NoOwner"
Controllers == {c1, c2}
Zones == {z1, z2}
Doors == {d1, d2}
DoorZone == (d1 :> z1) @@ (d2 :> z2)

VARIABLES zoneLock, doorLock, msgsZone, msgsDoor

vars == <<zoneLock, doorLock, msgsZone, msgsDoor>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ zoneLock \in [Zones -> Controllers \cup {NoOwner}]
  /\ doorLock \in [Doors -> Controllers \cup {NoOwner}]
  /\ msgsZone \subseteq [ctrl: Controllers, zone: Zones]
  /\ msgsDoor \subseteq [ctrl: Controllers, door: Doors]

Init ==
  /\ zoneLock = [z \in Zones |-> NoOwner]
  /\ doorLock = [d \in Doors |-> NoOwner]
  /\ msgsZone = {}
  /\ msgsDoor = {}

\* A controller sends a request to acquire a zone's coarse lock; the
\* request sits in an unordered set of pending messages.
RequestZone(c, z) ==
  /\ [ctrl |-> c, zone |-> z] \notin msgsZone
  /\ msgsZone' = msgsZone \cup {[ctrl |-> c, zone |-> z]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, doorLock, msgsDoor>>

\* The manager may grant ANY pending zone request next, not necessarily
\* the one sent first -- this is the reordering the network can introduce.
GrantZone ==
  /\ \E m \in msgsZone :
       /\ zoneLock[m.zone] = NoOwner
       /\ zoneLock' = [zoneLock EXCEPT ![m.zone] = m.ctrl]
       /\ msgsZone' = msgsZone \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<doorLock, msgsDoor>>

\* A controller sends a request to acquire a door's fine lock. Nothing
\* stops it from sending this before its zone request is even granted --
\* the network gives no ordering guarantee between the two.
RequestDoor(c, d) ==
  /\ [ctrl |-> c, door |-> d] \notin msgsDoor
  /\ msgsDoor' = msgsDoor \cup {[ctrl |-> c, door |-> d]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, doorLock, msgsZone>>

\* The manager grants a pending door request only if the CURRENT zone lock
\* (not the message's send order) shows this controller already owns the
\* door's zone -- this state-based re-check is what keeps hierarchical
\* mutual exclusion safe under message reordering.
GrantDoor ==
  /\ \E m \in msgsDoor :
       /\ doorLock[m.door] = NoOwner
       /\ zoneLock[DoorZone[m.door]] = m.ctrl
       /\ doorLock' = [doorLock EXCEPT ![m.door] = m.ctrl]
       /\ msgsDoor' = msgsDoor \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, msgsZone>>

\* A controller releases a door lock it holds.
ReleaseDoor(c, d) ==
  /\ doorLock[d] = c
  /\ doorLock' = [doorLock EXCEPT ![d] = NoOwner]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, msgsZone, msgsDoor>>

\* A controller may only release a zone lock once it no longer holds any
\* door lock inside that zone -- the hierarchical discipline that keeps
\* HierarchicalMutex from ever being violated by a release.
ReleaseZone(c, z) ==
  /\ zoneLock[z] = c
  /\ \A d \in Doors : DoorZone[d] = z => doorLock[d] # c
  /\ zoneLock' = [zoneLock EXCEPT ![z] = NoOwner]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<doorLock, msgsZone, msgsDoor>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, z \in Zones : RequestZone(c, z)
  \/ GrantZone
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, d \in Doors : RequestDoor(c, d)
  \/ GrantDoor
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, d \in Doors : ReleaseDoor(c, d)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, z \in Zones : ReleaseZone(c, z)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion of the critical resource (a door lock): whenever a
\* door is held by some controller, that controller must also hold the
\* coarse lock on the door's zone -- a stray or reordered grant can never
\* let a door lock exist without its matching exclusive zone ownership.
HierarchicalMutex == \A d \in Doors : doorLock[d] # NoOwner => zoneLock[DoorZone[d]] = doorLock[d]

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  c1 = c1
  c2 = c2
  z1 = z1
  z2 = z2
  d1 = d1
  d2 = d2
INVARIANT HierarchicalMutex
nl:
A smart-home door lock network is organized hierarchically: doors are
grouped into zones (for example, a "front" zone and a "back" zone), and a
controller app must hold a coarse lock on a zone before it may hold a
fine-grained lock on any individual door inside that zone. Requests to
acquire a lock are not delivered through a reliable, ordered channel --
they travel as messages sitting in an unordered pool, and the home's lock
manager may grant any pending request next, not necessarily the one a
controller sent first. In particular, a controller's door-acquire request
can be delivered and considered by the manager before its matching
zone-acquire request even arrives, because the network gives no ordering
guarantee between the two.

The mechanism survives this reordering because granting a door lock never
trusts the order requests arrived in: it re-checks, at the moment of
granting, whether the requesting controller currently owns the coarse lock
on that door's zone. If it does not -- even if the door request was sent
long after the zone request -- the grant simply does not happen yet, and
the request stays pending until the zone lock situation catches up.
Symmetrically, a controller is only allowed to release a zone's coarse
lock once it holds no door locks left inside that zone, so a release can
never strand a door lock without its matching zone ownership.

The full action set is: RequestZone (a controller sends a request to
acquire a zone's coarse lock, which sits in the unordered pool of pending
zone requests), GrantZone (the manager grants any pending zone request
whose zone is currently unlocked), RequestDoor (a controller sends a
request to acquire a specific door's fine lock, which sits in the
unordered pool of pending door requests -- possibly before its zone
request has even been granted), GrantDoor (the manager grants a pending
door request only if the requesting controller currently owns the coarse
lock on that door's zone), ReleaseDoor (a controller releases a door lock
it holds), and ReleaseZone (a controller releases a zone lock it holds,
but only once it holds none of that zone's door locks).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, whenever a door lock is held by
some controller, that same controller must also hold the coarse lock on
the door's zone -- reordered or out-of-order messages can never grant a
door lock to a controller that does not actually hold exclusive control of
its zone.
