---- MODULE W4Od16m2p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* A pharmacy dispenses a prescription only after a two-phase commit across
\* the participants that must all agree (inventory check, insurance check,
\* pharmacist license check) before the shared dispensing cabinet is
\* opened. Only one prescription negotiation runs at a time, and only that
\* prescription may hold the cabinet while dispensing -- CabinetMutex
\* checks that at most one prescription is ever in the dispensing state.
\* The twist: one designated participant (CrashProne) can go dark silently
\* mid-vote. Without recovery this would block the pending prescription in
\* "preparing" forever; TimeoutAbort lets the coordinator abort once it
\* detects the crash, so every prescription that starts negotiating is
\* still guaranteed to eventually reach a decision.

CONSTANTS Prescriptions, Participants, CrashProne
NoHolder == "NoHolder"

VARIABLES txState, votes, cabinetHolder, crashed

vars == <<txState, votes, cabinetHolder, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ txState \in [Prescriptions -> {"idle", "preparing", "dispensing", "aborted", "done"}]
  /\ votes \in [Prescriptions -> [Participants -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]]
  /\ cabinetHolder \in Prescriptions \cup {NoHolder}
  /\ crashed \subseteq {CrashProne}

Init ==
  /\ txState = [p \in Prescriptions |-> "idle"]
  /\ votes = [p \in Prescriptions |-> [q \in Participants |-> "none"]]
  /\ cabinetHolder = NoHolder
  /\ crashed = {}

\* Begin negotiating a prescription -- only when the pharmacy is not
\* already mid-negotiation on a different one.
StartPrepare(p) ==
  /\ txState[p] = "idle"
  /\ \A r \in Prescriptions \ {p} : txState[r] = "idle"
  /\ txState' = [txState EXCEPT ![p] = "preparing"]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = [q \in Participants |-> "none"]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinetHolder, crashed>>

\* A participant casts its 2PC vote on the prescription being negotiated.
Vote(p, q, v) ==
  /\ txState[p] = "preparing"
  /\ votes[p][q] = "none"
  /\ q \notin crashed
  /\ v \in {"yes", "no"}
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p][q] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<txState, cabinetHolder, crashed>>

\* All participants voted yes: the coordinator opens the cabinet
\* exclusively for this prescription.
Commit(p) ==
  /\ txState[p] = "preparing"
  /\ \A q \in Participants : votes[p][q] = "yes"
  /\ cabinetHolder = NoHolder
  /\ txState' = [txState EXCEPT ![p] = "dispensing"]
  /\ cabinetHolder' = p
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, crashed>>

\* Some participant voted no: the prescription is aborted.
Abort(p) ==
  /\ txState[p] = "preparing"
  /\ \E q \in Participants : votes[p][q] = "no"
  /\ txState' = [txState EXCEPT ![p] = "aborted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, cabinetHolder, crashed>>

\* The coordinator detects that CrashProne has gone silent mid-vote and
\* aborts rather than blocking the prescription forever.
TimeoutAbort(p) ==
  /\ txState[p] = "preparing"
  /\ CrashProne \in crashed
  /\ votes[p][CrashProne] = "none"
  /\ txState' = [txState EXCEPT ![p] = "aborted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, cabinetHolder, crashed>>

\* The holder finishes dispensing and gives up the cabinet.
Finish(p) ==
  /\ txState[p] = "dispensing"
  /\ cabinetHolder = p
  /\ txState' = [txState EXCEPT ![p] = "done"]
  /\ cabinetHolder' = NoHolder
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, crashed>>

\* A resolved prescription slot is cleared so the pharmacy can negotiate
\* the next one (or a refill of the same one).
Reissue(p) ==
  /\ txState[p] \in {"aborted", "done"}
  /\ txState' = [txState EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, cabinetHolder, crashed>>

\* Twist: the designated participant crashes silently, without warning,
\* and never votes again.
CrashParticipant ==
  /\ CrashProne \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {CrashProne}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<txState, votes, cabinetHolder>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Prescriptions : StartPrepare(p)
  \/ \E p \in Prescriptions, q \in Participants, v \in {"yes", "no"} : Vote(p, q, v)
  \/ \E p \in Prescriptions : Commit(p)
  \/ \E p \in Prescriptions : Abort(p)
  \/ \E p \in Prescriptions : TimeoutAbort(p)
  \/ \E p \in Prescriptions : Finish(p)
  \/ \E p \in Prescriptions : Reissue(p)
  \/ CrashParticipant

VoteAny(p, q) == \E v \in {"yes", "no"} : Vote(p, q, v)
ResolveStep(p) == Commit(p) \/ Abort(p) \/ TimeoutAbort(p)

Fairness ==
  /\ \A p \in Prescriptions, q \in Participants : WF_vars(VoteAny(p, q))
  /\ \A p \in Prescriptions : WF_vars(ResolveStep(p))
  /\ \A p \in Prescriptions : WF_vars(Finish(p))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* ever actually dispensing from the shared cabinet at a time.
CabinetMutex == Cardinality({p \in Prescriptions : txState[p] = "dispensing"}) <= 1

\* Liveness: a prescription that begins negotiating a two-phase commit
\* always eventually leaves the "preparing" state -- the crash-prone
\* participant going silent can delay but never permanently block it.
EventualResolution == \A p \in Prescriptions : (txState[p] = "preparing") ~> (txState[p] # "preparing")

  Participants = {q1, q2}
  CrashProne = q1

nl:
A pharmacy dispenses prescriptions from a single shared dispensing cabinet.
Before the cabinet opens for a prescription, the pharmacy runs a two-phase
commit across the participants that all have to sign off -- an inventory
check, an insurance check, and a pharmacist license check. Each participant
independently votes yes or no; if every participant votes yes, the
coordinator commits and the cabinet opens exclusively for that
prescription; if any participant votes no, the prescription is aborted.
Only one prescription is negotiated at a time, and it is the only
prescription ever actually allowed to hold the cabinet open (dispensing) --
no other prescription may be dispensing from the shared cabinet while it is
still in use.

The twist is that one of the participants is known to be prone to going
silent: it can crash without warning at any point, including in the middle
of a vote, and once it is gone it never casts another vote. Without a
recovery path, a prescription waiting on that participant's vote would be
stuck in "preparing" forever, permanently occupying the pharmacy's single
negotiation slot. Instead, once the coordinator detects the participant has
gone dark, it aborts the pending prescription via a timeout rather than
waiting on a vote that will never come, freeing the pharmacy to move on to
the next prescription.

The full action set is: StartPrepare (the pharmacy begins negotiating a
prescription, only when no other prescription is currently mid-negotiation),
Vote (a participant casts its yes/no vote on the prescription being
negotiated), Commit (all participants voted yes, so the coordinator opens
the cabinet exclusively for this prescription), Abort (some participant
voted no, so the prescription is aborted), TimeoutAbort (the coordinator
detects the crash-prone participant has gone silent mid-vote and aborts
rather than waiting forever), Finish (the current holder finishes
dispensing and gives up the cabinet), Reissue (a resolved prescription
slot is cleared so the pharmacy can negotiate the next one), and
CrashParticipant (the designated participant crashes silently and never
votes again).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, at most one prescription is
ever actually dispensing from the shared cabinet at a time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: A prescription that begins two-phase-commit negotiation
always eventually leaves the "preparing" state -- the crash-prone
participant going silent can delay a decision but never permanently block
it.

---- MODULE W4Od4m2p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* A car-wash conveyor line assigns each car to a bay slot only after a
\* two-phase commit across the participants that both must sign off (the
\* schedule controller and the payment terminal): a car proposes a slot,
\* both participants vote, and only if every vote is yes -- and the slot is
\* still online and still unclaimed by any other car -- does the
\* allocation actually commit. The twist is that the number of usable bays
\* changes at runtime: a bay can be taken offline for maintenance or
\* brought back online at any time, even while a car's proposal for it is
\* still in flight. NoDoubleAllocation checks that no two different cars
\* ever end up holding the same committed slot, regardless of how capacity
\* churns underneath a pending negotiation.

CONSTANTS Cars, Slots, Participants
NoSlot == "NoSlot"

VARIABLES committed, proposal, votes, online

vars == <<committed, proposal, votes, online>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ committed \in [Cars -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ proposal \in [Cars -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ votes \in [Cars -> [Participants -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]]
  /\ online \subseteq Slots

Init ==
  /\ committed = [c \in Cars |-> NoSlot]
  /\ proposal = [c \in Cars |-> NoSlot]
  /\ votes = [c \in Cars |-> [q \in Participants |-> "none"]]
  /\ online = Slots

\* A car proposes a candidate bay slot for its wash. The final occupancy
\* check happens at commit time, not here.
Propose(c, s) ==
  /\ committed[c] = NoSlot
  /\ proposal[c] = NoSlot
  /\ s \in online
  /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![c] = s]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![c] = [q \in Participants |-> "none"]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, online>>

\* A participant casts its 2PC vote on the car's proposed slot.
Vote(c, q, v) ==
  /\ proposal[c] # NoSlot
  /\ votes[c][q] = "none"
  /\ v \in {"yes", "no"}
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![c][q] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, proposal, online>>

\* Both participants voted yes: the allocation only actually commits if
\* the slot is still online and still unclaimed by any other car -- this
\* re-check is what stands between the model and a double allocation.
Commit(c) ==
  /\ proposal[c] # NoSlot
  /\ \A q \in Participants : votes[c][q] = "yes"
  /\ proposal[c] \in online
  /\ \A c2 \in Cars \ {c} : committed[c2] # proposal[c]
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![c] = proposal[c]]
  /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![c] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, online>>

\* A participant voted no, or the re-check at commit time would fail: the
\* proposal is dropped so the car can try again.
Abort(c) ==
  /\ proposal[c] # NoSlot
  /\ \/ \E q \in Participants : votes[c][q] = "no"
     \/ proposal[c] \notin online
     \/ \E c2 \in Cars \ {c} : committed[c2] = proposal[c]
  /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![c] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, votes, online>>

\* The car finishes its wash and frees the bay slot.
Release(c) ==
  /\ committed[c] # NoSlot
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![c] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, votes, online>>

\* Twist: a bay is taken offline for maintenance -- only a slot no car is
\* currently committed to can go offline, but a slot with only a pending,
\* uncommitted proposal can still be pulled out from under it.
TakeOffline(s) ==
  /\ s \in online
  /\ \A c \in Cars : committed[c] # s
  /\ online' = online \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, proposal, votes>>

\* Twist: a bay is brought back into service.
BringOnline(s) ==
  /\ s \notin online
  /\ online' = online \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, proposal, votes>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars, s \in Slots : Propose(c, s)
  \/ \E c \in Cars, q \in Participants, v \in {"yes", "no"} : Vote(c, q, v)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Commit(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Abort(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Release(c)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : TakeOffline(s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : BringOnline(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation of the same slot: no two distinct cars are ever
\* both committed to the same bay slot at once.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A c1, c2 \in Cars :
    (c1 # c2 /\ committed[c1] # NoSlot /\ committed[c2] # NoSlot) => committed[c1] # committed[c2]

====
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has a small number of bay slots that cars pass
through while being washed. Assigning a car to a bay is not a simple
write: it goes through a two-phase commit across the two participants that
both have to sign off before the assignment is real -- the schedule
controller (which tracks the conveyor's timing) and the payment terminal
(which confirms the customer has paid). A car proposes a candidate bay,
both participants independently vote yes or no, and only if both vote yes
does the assignment attempt move to commit. At commit time the system
re-checks, from scratch, whether the bay is still in service and still
unclaimed by any other car -- because a lot can change while the vote was
in flight.

That re-check matters because of the twist: the number of usable bays on
the line changes at runtime. Bays go offline for maintenance and come back
online as staff take stations down or bring them back up, and this can
happen at any time, including while some car's proposal for that exact bay
is still waiting on votes. A bay can even be pulled offline out from under
a pending (not yet committed) proposal. The only thing that is never
allowed to happen is two different cars both ending up actually committed
to the same bay slot at the same time.

The full action set is: Propose (a car proposes a candidate bay slot,
only if the bay is currently online), Vote (a participant casts its
yes/no vote on a car's proposed bay), Commit (both participants voted
yes, and the bay is re-checked as still online and still unclaimed by any
other car, so the allocation becomes real), Abort (a participant voted
no, or the bay is no longer online, or another car already holds it, so
the proposal is dropped), Release (a car finishes its wash and frees its
bay slot), TakeOffline (a bay with no car currently committed to it is
taken out of service for maintenance), and BringOnline (an offline bay is
brought back into service).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, no two distinct cars are ever
both committed to the same bay slot at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od15m4p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* A stock exchange opening auction stages incoming broker orders in a
\* bounded work queue (Submit is refused once the queue is at capacity --
\* backpressure). The queue is modeled as an unordered set, not a FIFO
\* sequence, because messages between brokers and the matching engine can
\* be reordered in transit: the engine may pick up and match any pending
\* order next, and a cancellation can likewise land ahead of or behind a
\* submission with no fixed ordering. Only one worker may hold the
\* matching engine's exclusive write access to the shared order book at a
\* time. EngineMutex checks that at most one worker ever holds it.

CONSTANTS Orders, Workers, Cap

VARIABLES pending, holding, processed, cancelled

vars == <<pending, holding, processed, cancelled>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ pending \subseteq Orders
  /\ Cardinality(pending) <= Cap
  /\ holding \subseteq Workers
  /\ processed \subseteq Orders
  /\ cancelled \subseteq Orders

Init ==
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ holding = {}
  /\ processed = {}
  /\ cancelled = {}

\* A broker submits an order into the bounded queue; backpressure refuses
\* it once the queue is already at capacity.
Submit(o) ==
  /\ o \notin pending
  /\ Cardinality(pending) < Cap
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holding, processed, cancelled>>

\* A worker grabs exclusive access to the matching engine. Because pending
\* is unordered, which order it will match next is not determined by
\* submission order.
AcquireEngine(w) ==
  /\ holding = {}
  /\ pending # {}
  /\ holding' = {w}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, processed, cancelled>>

\* The worker holding the engine matches one pending order -- any pending
\* order, reflecting that message delivery order is not preserved.
ProcessOrder(w, o) ==
  /\ holding = {w}
  /\ o \in pending
  /\ pending' = pending \ {o}
  /\ processed' = processed \cup {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holding, cancelled>>

\* The worker releases the matching engine.
ReleaseEngine(w) ==
  /\ holding = {w}
  /\ holding' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, processed, cancelled>>

\* A broker cancels a still-pending order; this message, too, can arrive
\* in any order relative to submissions and matches.
Cancel(o) ==
  /\ o \in pending
  /\ pending' = pending \ {o}
  /\ cancelled' = cancelled \cup {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holding, processed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E o \in Orders : Submit(o)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : AcquireEngine(w)
  \/ \E w \in Workers, o \in Orders : ProcessOrder(w, o)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : ReleaseEngine(w)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : Cancel(o)

\* An order always has a way out of the queue -- being matched or being
\* cancelled -- regardless of how engine contention or message reordering
\* plays out around it.
AdvanceStep(o) == Cancel(o) \/ (\E w \in Workers : ProcessOrder(w, o))

Fairness == \A o \in Orders : WF_vars(AdvanceStep(o))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* Mutual exclusion of the critical resource: at most one worker ever
\* holds exclusive write access to the shared order book at a time.
EngineMutex == Cardinality(holding) <= 1

\* Liveness: every order accepted into the bounded queue eventually leaves
\* it, whether by being matched or by being cancelled -- nothing sits in
\* the queue forever even though delivery order is not guaranteed.
EventualResolution == \A o \in Orders : (o \in pending) ~> (o \notin pending)

CONSTANTS
  Orders = {o1, o2, o3}
  Workers = {w1, w2}
  Cap = 2
INVARIANT EngineMutex
PROPERTY EventualResolution
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction where broker orders are staged in
a bounded work queue before the matching engine processes them against the
shared order book. The queue enforces backpressure: once it is already at
capacity, a new order submission is refused outright rather than being
buffered without limit. Critically, the queue is not a reliable ordered
channel -- messages between brokers and the matching engine can be
reordered in transit, so the engine may pick up and match any currently
pending order next, not necessarily the one submitted first, and a
cancellation message can likewise land ahead of or behind a submission
with no fixed ordering guarantee.

Only one worker thread may hold exclusive write access to the shared order
book at a time -- while a worker is matching an order, no other worker may
touch the book. A worker must explicitly acquire this exclusive access
before it may match a pending order, and must release it afterward before
any other worker can acquire it.

The full action set is: Submit (a broker submits an order into the bounded
queue, refused once the queue is at capacity), AcquireEngine (a worker
grabs exclusive access to the matching engine, only when nobody else
currently holds it), ProcessOrder (the worker holding the engine matches
one pending order -- any pending order, since delivery order is not
preserved), ReleaseEngine (the worker releases exclusive access to the
engine), and Cancel (a broker cancels a still-pending order, a message
that can itself arrive out of order relative to submissions and matches).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, at most one worker thread ever
holds exclusive access to the shared order book at a time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every order accepted into the bounded queue eventually
leaves it, either because it is matched by the engine or because it is
cancelled -- no accepted order sits in the queue forever, even though
message delivery order between brokers and the engine is not guaranteed.

---- MODULE W4Od16m8p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, TLC

\* A pharmacy prescription dispenser organizes its medication bins inside
\* storage cabinets. Filling a prescription from a specific bin requires a
\* pharmacist to first hold coarse access to the bin's cabinet, then
\* request and be granted the fine-grained allocation of that bin slot
\* (hierarchical locking used purely as the access-control mechanism). The
\* twist is that one designated pharmacist, CrashProne, can go silent at
\* any point -- including while holding cabinet access or bin allocations
\* -- and a supervisor action is the only way to reclaim what it was
\* holding. NoDoubleAllocation checks the actual property of interest:
\* no bin slot is ever allocated to two different pharmacists at once,
\* no matter how the crash-and-reclaim path plays out.

CONSTANTS p1, p2, c1, c2, b1, b2
NoOwner == "NoOwner"
Pharmacists == {p1, p2}
Cabinets == {c1, c2}
Bins == {b1, b2}
BinCabinet == (b1 :> c1) @@ (b2 :> c2)
CrashProne == p1

VARIABLES cabinetLock, requested, allocated, crashed

vars == <<cabinetLock, requested, allocated, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ cabinetLock \in [Cabinets -> Pharmacists \cup {NoOwner}]
  /\ requested \subseteq (Pharmacists \X Bins)
  /\ allocated \subseteq (Pharmacists \X Bins)
  /\ crashed \subseteq {CrashProne}

Init ==
  /\ cabinetLock = [c \in Cabinets |-> NoOwner]
  /\ requested = {}
  /\ allocated = {}
  /\ crashed = {}

\* A pharmacist takes coarse access to a cabinet, needed before any bin
\* slot inside it can be allocated to them.
AcquireCabinet(p, c) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ cabinetLock[c] = NoOwner
  /\ cabinetLock' = [cabinetLock EXCEPT ![c] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<requested, allocated, crashed>>

\* A pharmacist asks for a specific bin slot to fill a prescription from.
RequestBin(p, b) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ <<p, b>> \notin requested
  /\ <<p, b>> \notin allocated
  /\ requested' = requested \cup {<<p, b>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinetLock, allocated, crashed>>

\* The dispenser grants the bin allocation only if the pharmacist already
\* holds the cabinet's coarse access AND no one else currently holds this
\* exact bin slot -- the guard that keeps allocation free of double-booking.
GrantBin(p, b) ==
  /\ <<p, b>> \in requested
  /\ cabinetLock[BinCabinet[b]] = p
  /\ \A p2v \in Pharmacists : <<p2v, b>> \notin allocated
  /\ allocated' = allocated \cup {<<p, b>>}
  /\ requested' = requested \ {<<p, b>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinetLock, crashed>>

\* A pharmacist gives back a bin slot allocation once the fill is done.
ReleaseBin(p, b) ==
  /\ <<p, b>> \in allocated
  /\ allocated' = allocated \ {<<p, b>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinetLock, requested, crashed>>

\* A pharmacist releases coarse cabinet access, only once none of that
\* cabinet's bin slots are still allocated to them.
ReleaseCabinet(p, c) ==
  /\ cabinetLock[c] = p
  /\ \A b \in Bins : BinCabinet[b] = c => <<p, b>> \notin allocated
  /\ cabinetLock' = [cabinetLock EXCEPT ![c] = NoOwner]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<requested, allocated, crashed>>

\* Twist: the one crash-prone pharmacist goes silent without warning,
\* possibly while still holding cabinet access or bin allocations.
CrashSilently ==
  /\ CrashProne \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {CrashProne}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinetLock, requested, allocated>>

\* A supervisor reclaims everything the crashed pharmacist was holding
\* under one cabinet -- its coarse access and any bin slots it had
\* allocated there -- so the cabinet and its bins are not lost forever.
SupervisorReclaim(c) ==
  /\ cabinetLock[c] = CrashProne
  /\ CrashProne \in crashed
  /\ cabinetLock' = [cabinetLock EXCEPT ![c] = NoOwner]
  /\ allocated' = {pr \in allocated : ~(pr[1] = CrashProne /\ BinCabinet[pr[2]] = c)}
  /\ requested' = {pr \in requested : ~(pr[1] = CrashProne /\ BinCabinet[pr[2]] = c)}
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists, c \in Cabinets : AcquireCabinet(p, c)
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists, b \in Bins : RequestBin(p, b)
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists, b \in Bins : GrantBin(p, b)
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists, b \in Bins : ReleaseBin(p, b)
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists, c \in Cabinets : ReleaseCabinet(p, c)
  \/ CrashSilently
  \/ \E c \in Cabinets : SupervisorReclaim(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation of the same slot: for every bin, at most one
\* pharmacist holds an active allocation of it at any reachable state.
NoDoubleAllocation == \A b \in Bins : Cardinality({p \in Pharmacists : <<p, b>> \in allocated}) <= 1

CONSTANTS
  p1 = p1
  p2 = p2
  c1 = c1
  c2 = c2
  b1 = b1
  b2 = b2
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A pharmacy's automated dispenser organizes medication bins inside a small
number of storage cabinets. Filling a prescription from a specific bin
slot is a two-step access process: a pharmacist first takes coarse access
to the bin's cabinet, then requests that a specific bin slot inside it be
allocated to them. The dispenser only grants that allocation if the
pharmacist already holds the cabinet's coarse access and nobody else
currently has that exact bin slot allocated -- the whole point of the
two-step process is to make sure a bin slot is never handed out to two
different pharmacists' fills at once.

The twist is that one designated pharmacist on staff is known to be
unreliable: it can go silent without warning at any point, whether it is
holding nothing, holding coarse access to a cabinet, or holding one or
more bin-slot allocations inside it. A silent pharmacist cannot release
anything itself, so a supervisor step exists specifically to sweep up
after it -- reclaiming both the crashed pharmacist's coarse cabinet access
and any bin slots it had allocated inside that cabinet, all in one
corrective step, so the cabinet and its bins are never permanently
stranded.

The full action set is: AcquireCabinet (a pharmacist takes coarse access
to an unheld cabinet), RequestBin (a pharmacist asks for a specific bin
slot inside a cabinet), GrantBin (the dispenser allocates the bin slot to
the requesting pharmacist, but only if they hold the cabinet's coarse
access and nobody else currently holds that slot), ReleaseBin (a
pharmacist gives back a bin-slot allocation once its fill is done),
ReleaseCabinet (a pharmacist releases coarse cabinet access, only once
none of that cabinet's bin slots are still allocated to them),
CrashSilently (the one unreliable pharmacist goes silent without warning,
possibly mid-fill), and SupervisorReclaim (a supervisor sweeps up
everything the crashed pharmacist was holding under one cabinet -- its
coarse access and any bin allocations -- in a single corrective step).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, no bin slot is ever allocated
to more than one pharmacist at the same time, whether or not the
crash-and-reclaim path has been exercised.

---- MODULE W4Od7m4p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Containers, Cranes, Capacity, NoContainer

VARIABLES pending, queue, claimed, lifted, crashed

vars == <<pending, queue, claimed, lifted, crashed>>

\* A crane yard runs a bounded intake queue: containers wait in `pending`
\* until there is room in `queue` (backpressure keyed on Capacity), then a
\* crane claims the queue head and lifts it onto a ship -- lifting is
\* irreversible and must happen at most once per container.  Exactly one
\* crane may crash silently while holding a claimed container; a live
\* crane later requeues that stranded container so the yard still drains.

QueueSet == {queue[i] : i \in DOMAIN queue}

Init ==
  /\ pending = Containers
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ claimed = [k \in Cranes |-> NoContainer]
  /\ lifted = {}
  /\ crashed = {}

Enqueue(c) ==
  /\ c \in pending
  /\ Len(queue) < Capacity
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, c)
  /\ pending' = pending \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<claimed, lifted, crashed>>

ClaimK(k) ==
  /\ k \notin crashed
  /\ claimed[k] = NoContainer
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![k] = Head(queue)]
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, lifted, crashed>>

LiftK(k) ==
  /\ k \notin crashed
  /\ claimed[k] # NoContainer
  /\ lifted' = lifted \cup {claimed[k]}
  /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![k] = NoContainer]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, queue, crashed>>

Crash(k) ==
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ crashed' = {k}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, queue, claimed, lifted>>

RequeueK(k) ==
  /\ k \in crashed
  /\ claimed[k] # NoContainer
  /\ queue' = <<claimed[k]>> \o queue
  /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![k] = NoContainer]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, lifted, crashed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Containers : Enqueue(c)
  \/ \E k \in Cranes : ClaimK(k) \/ LiftK(k) \/ Crash(k) \/ RequeueK(k)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A c \in Containers : WF_vars(Enqueue(c))
  /\ \A k \in Cranes : WF_vars(ClaimK(k)) /\ WF_vars(LiftK(k)) /\ WF_vars(RequeueK(k))

\* Once a container has been lifted it can never again be waiting, queued,
\* or claimed -- so the Lift action can never fire a second time on it.
NoDoubleLift ==
  \A c \in Containers :
    c \in lifted => /\ c \notin pending
                     /\ c \notin QueueSet
                     /\ \A k \in Cranes : claimed[k] # c

AllContainersEventuallyLifted == <>(lifted = Containers)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Containers = {c1, c2, c3}
  Cranes = {k1, k2}
  Capacity = 2
  NoContainer = NoContainer
INVARIANT NoDoubleLift
PROPERTY AllContainersEventuallyLifted
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A container-ship crane yard runs a bounded intake queue for outbound cargo.
Containers destined for a departing ship start out sitting in a holding lot
(`pending`); dock coordinators can only move a container into the active
work queue when the queue has spare slots -- this is the backpressure
mechanism, bounded by the constant Capacity, that keeps the crane operators
from being swamped with more claimed work than they can track. Cranes pull
containers off the head of that queue, claim them, and then lift them onto
the ship. Lifting a container onto the ship is the irreversible action in
this system: once a container has been swung aboard it can never be handed
back to a crane or re-queued, and it must happen exactly once per container.

Because crane-yard hardware occasionally locks up without warning, the model
allows exactly one crane to crash silently while it is holding a claimed
container. A crashed crane simply stops issuing lifts -- it does not corrupt
the queue or duplicate the lift -- but its stranded container would sit
forever unless a surviving crane notices and requeues it. Requeuing pushes
the stranded container back to the front of the queue so a live crane can
claim it and finish the job.

The full action set is: Enqueue(c) -- move a pending container into the
queue when there is spare capacity; ClaimK(k) -- a non-crashed crane k pulls
the head of the queue into its own hands; LiftK(k) -- a non-crashed crane k
swings its claimed container aboard the ship, marking it lifted forever;
Crash(k) -- crane k silently fails (allowed for at most one crane in the
whole run); and RequeueK(k) -- a crashed crane's stranded claimed container
is pushed back onto the queue so another crane can pick it up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A container that has already been lifted is never again
present in the pending lot, the work queue, or any crane's claimed slot, so
no container can ever be lifted a second time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every container eventually gets lifted onto the ship,
even though up to one crane may crash silently partway through handling it.

---- MODULE W4Od3m3p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Updates, MaxCapacity, MaxTerm, NoLeader

VARIABLES leader, term, pending, applied, capacity, everSubmitted

vars == <<leader, term, pending, applied, capacity, everSubmitted>>

\* An interbank settlement batch elects one bank as leader (with failover
\* via re-election at a fresh, higher term) to apply queued settlement
\* updates into the shared ledger record.  The queue's admission capacity
\* can be resized at runtime by the active leader; a shrink only throttles
\* new admissions and must never cause an already-admitted update to be
\* silently dropped before it is applied -- that is the "no lost updates"
\* guarantee the invariant below checks.

Init ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ term = 0
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ applied = {}
  /\ capacity = MaxCapacity
  /\ everSubmitted = {}

Elect(n) ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ leader' = n
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, applied, capacity, everSubmitted>>

StepDown ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ leader' = NoLeader
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, pending, applied, capacity, everSubmitted>>

Submit(u) ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ u \notin pending
  /\ u \notin applied
  /\ Cardinality(pending) < capacity
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {u}
  /\ everSubmitted' = everSubmitted \cup {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, applied, capacity>>

Apply(u) ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ u \in pending
  /\ applied' = applied \cup {u}
  /\ pending' = pending \ {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, capacity, everSubmitted>>

Reconfigure(newCap) ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ newCap \in 1..MaxCapacity
  /\ capacity' = newCap
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, pending, applied, everSubmitted>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
  \/ StepDown
  \/ \E u \in Updates : Submit(u) \/ Apply(u)
  \/ \E newCap \in 1..MaxCapacity : Reconfigure(newCap)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No settlement update, once admitted into the batch, is ever lost: it
\* remains either queued or applied to the ledger, regardless of leader
\* failover or a runtime capacity shrink.
NoLostUpdates == everSubmitted \subseteq (pending \cup applied)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Nodes = {n1, n2}
  Updates = {u1, u2, u3}
  MaxCapacity = 2
  MaxTerm = 3
  NoLeader = NoLeader
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A group of banks runs a shared interbank settlement batch: once per cycle
they need one bank to act as batch leader and fold a queue of pending
settlement updates into the shared ledger record. Leadership is decided by
election, and because a leader can go offline mid-cycle (a network partition,
a maintenance restart), the batch supports failover: once the current leader
steps down, any bank can be elected as the new leader at a fresh, strictly
higher term, so stale leaders never get confused with the live one.

While a leader is active, member banks submit settlement updates into an
admission queue, but the queue only accepts a new update while it has spare
room under the batch's admission capacity. That capacity is not fixed: the
active leader can reconfigure it up or down at runtime, for example shrinking
it during a risk event to slow the pace of new admissions. Crucially, shrinking
capacity only throttles future submissions -- it must never cause an update
that was already admitted into the queue to be discarded before the leader
gets a chance to apply it to the ledger. That is the core safety concern:
no interbank update, once accepted, may ever be lost, whether because of a
leader failover or because of a runtime capacity change.

The full action set is: Elect(n) -- bank n is elected leader whenever there
is currently no leader, starting a new, higher term; StepDown -- the active
leader goes offline and leadership becomes vacant, opening the door for a
new election; Submit(u) -- a member bank admits settlement update u into the
pending queue, guarded by the current capacity; Apply(u) -- the active leader
folds a pending update into the shared ledger record, moving it from pending
to applied; and Reconfigure(newCap) -- the active leader resizes the batch's
admission capacity at runtime, which only affects future Submit calls.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every settlement update that has ever been admitted into the
batch remains either in the pending queue or already applied to the ledger
record forever afterward -- it can never silently vanish, regardless of
leader failover or a runtime capacity change.

---- MODULE W4Od11m7p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Jobs, Printers, NoPrinter

VARIABLES unreleased, slot, owner, crashed

vars == <<unreleased, slot, owner, crashed>>

\* A print-shop job spooler holds each job's lifecycle in a per-job
\* compare-and-swap register `slot`, numbered 0=Unreleased, 1=Free,
\* 2=Claimed, 3=Printed. A printer CASes a job from Free to its own id to
\* claim it, then CASes Claimed to Printed -- printing is irreversible and
\* no action ever transitions a job's register away from 3. Exactly one
\* printer may crash silently while holding a claim; a surviving printer's
\* CAS then resets that job's register back to Free for reassignment.
\* The invariant checks that the register value and its owner metadata
\* never drift out of sync, which is what makes the CAS swaps trustworthy.

Init ==
  /\ unreleased = Jobs
  /\ slot = [j \in Jobs |-> 0]
  /\ owner = [j \in Jobs |-> NoPrinter]
  /\ crashed = {}

Release(j) ==
  /\ j \in unreleased
  /\ unreleased' = unreleased \ {j}
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![j] = 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, crashed>>

Claim(k, j) ==
  /\ k \notin crashed
  /\ slot[j] = 1
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![j] = 2]
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<unreleased, crashed>>

Print(k, j) ==
  /\ k \notin crashed
  /\ slot[j] = 2
  /\ owner[j] = k
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![j] = 3]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<unreleased, owner, crashed>>

Crash(k) ==
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ crashed' = {k}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<unreleased, slot, owner>>

Recover(k, j) ==
  /\ k \in crashed
  /\ slot[j] = 2
  /\ owner[j] = k
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![j] = 1]
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j] = NoPrinter]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<unreleased, crashed>>

ClaimK(k) == \E j \in Jobs : Claim(k, j)
PrintK(k) == \E j \in Jobs : Print(k, j)
RecoverK(k) == \E j \in Jobs : Recover(k, j)
ReleaseAny == \E j \in Jobs : Release(j)

Next ==
  \/ ReleaseAny
  \/ \E k \in Printers, j \in Jobs : Claim(k, j) \/ Print(k, j) \/ Recover(k, j)
  \/ \E k \in Printers : Crash(k)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(ReleaseAny)
  /\ \A k \in Printers : WF_vars(ClaimK(k)) /\ WF_vars(PrintK(k)) /\ WF_vars(RecoverK(k))

\* The CAS register's value and its ownership metadata always agree: a job
\* is claimed-or-printed exactly when it has a real owner, and it is
\* free-or-unreleased exactly when it has none.  A guard bug that let a
\* claim or a reprint slip through with stale ownership would break this.
RegisterOwnershipCoherent ==
  \A j \in Jobs :
    /\ (slot[j] \in {2, 3}) <=> (owner[j] \in Printers)
    /\ (slot[j] \in {0, 1}) <=> (owner[j] = NoPrinter)

AllJobsEventuallyPrinted == <>(\A j \in Jobs : slot[j] = 3)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Jobs = {j1, j2, j3}
  Printers = {p1, p2}
  NoPrinter = NoPrinter
INVARIANT RegisterOwnershipCoherent
PROPERTY AllJobsEventuallyPrinted
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A print shop runs a job spooler where every incoming job is tracked by its
own compare-and-swap register instead of a global lock. Each job's register
holds a small numeric state: Unreleased while it is still sitting in the
spooler's backlog, Free once the spooler has released it for printing,
Claimed once a printer has CASed it to their own id, and Printed once that
printer has finished the irreversible act of running it through the press.
Because printing physically consumes paper and toner, it must happen at most
once per job -- the register never transitions away from Printed once it
gets there, so no job can accidentally be rerun.

Printers occasionally lock up without warning while they are still holding a
claimed job. The model allows exactly one printer to crash silently. When
that happens, its claimed job's register is stuck at Claimed with that dead
printer listed as owner, until a surviving printer's compare-and-swap resets
the register back to Free -- at which point any live printer, including the
one that recovers it, may claim and print it as normal.

The full action set is: Release(j) -- the spooler releases job j from its
backlog, CASing its register from Unreleased to Free; Claim(k, j) -- a
non-crashed printer k CASes job j's register from Free to Claimed and
records itself as owner; Print(k, j) -- the owning, non-crashed printer k
CASes job j's register from Claimed to Printed, the irreversible action;
Crash(k) -- printer k silently fails while it may still be holding a claim
(allowed for at most one printer in the whole run); and Recover(k, j) -- a
job claimed by a now-crashed printer k has its register CASed back from
Claimed to Free, with ownership cleared, so another printer can pick it up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A job's register and its recorded owner are always
consistent -- the register reads Claimed or Printed exactly when the job has
a real printer owner, and reads Unreleased or Free exactly when it has none
-- so a job can never be printed by CAS transitions that skip or repeat the
Claimed-to-Printed step.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every job in the shop is eventually printed, even though
up to one printer may crash silently while holding a claim.

---- MODULE W4Od3m5p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Slots, Voters, Quorum, NoOwner

VARIABLES allocated, proposer, votes, adminUsed

vars == <<allocated, proposer, votes, adminUsed>>

\* An interbank settlement batch has a fixed pool of settlement slots that
\* member banks must acquire before writing to them.  Ordinarily a bank
\* proposes itself for a slot and other banks cast votes; only once a
\* quorum of votes is reached does the slot actually become allocated.  A
\* privileged compliance admin can bypass the vote entirely and force an
\* allocation straight through -- but that override is capped at once per
\* slot, and it must still leave the slot held by exactly one bank.  The
\* invariant checks that no slot is ever held by more than one bank at a
\* time, whether it got there by quorum or by admin override.

Init ==
  /\ allocated = {}
  /\ proposer = [s \in Slots |-> NoOwner]
  /\ votes = [s \in Slots |-> {}]
  /\ adminUsed = {}

SlotFree(s) == \A v \in Voters : <<s, v>> \notin allocated

Propose(s, v) ==
  /\ SlotFree(s)
  /\ proposer[s] = NoOwner
  /\ v \in Voters
  /\ proposer' = [proposer EXCEPT ![s] = v]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<allocated, adminUsed>>

Vote(s, v) ==
  /\ proposer[s] # NoOwner
  /\ v \notin votes[s]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = votes[s] \cup {v}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<allocated, proposer, adminUsed>>

Commit(s) ==
  /\ proposer[s] # NoOwner
  /\ Cardinality(votes[s]) >= Quorum
  /\ SlotFree(s)
  /\ allocated' = allocated \cup {<<s, proposer[s]>>}
  /\ proposer' = [proposer EXCEPT ![s] = NoOwner]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED adminUsed

Release(s, v) ==
  /\ <<s, v>> \in allocated
  /\ allocated' = allocated \ {<<s, v>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposer, votes, adminUsed>>

\* The admin override skips voting entirely and can even displace a bank
\* that already holds the slot, but it always clears the old holder before
\* installing the new one, and it can only be invoked once per slot.
AdminOverride(s, v) ==
  /\ s \notin adminUsed
  /\ v \in Voters
  /\ allocated' = {<<s, v>>} \cup {p \in allocated : p[1] # s}
  /\ proposer' = [proposer EXCEPT ![s] = NoOwner]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ adminUsed' = adminUsed \cup {s}

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Slots, v \in Voters : Propose(s, v) \/ Vote(s, v) \/ Release(s, v) \/ AdminOverride(s, v)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Commit(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No settlement slot is ever concurrently held by more than one bank,
\* regardless of whether it was acquired through a full quorum vote or
\* pushed through by the privileged admin override.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A s \in Slots : Cardinality({v \in Voters : <<s, v>> \in allocated}) <= 1

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Slots = {s1, s2}
  Voters = {v1, v2, v3}
  Quorum = 2
  NoOwner = NoOwner
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A consortium of banks runs an interbank settlement batch built around a
fixed pool of settlement slots -- each slot represents a specific ledger
write window that only one bank may hold at a time while it posts its
settlement entries. Ordinarily, acquiring a slot goes through quorum
voting: a bank proposes itself as the candidate holder of a slot, other
member banks cast votes for that candidacy, and only once enough votes
accumulate to reach the consortium's quorum threshold does the slot
actually become allocated to the proposer. This keeps any single bank
from unilaterally grabbing a slot.

For emergencies -- a stuck settlement window near a regulatory deadline,
say -- the consortium also grants one privileged compliance admin the
power to override the vote entirely and force a slot straight to a bank of
its choosing, cancelling any in-flight vote for that slot in the process.
The override is deliberately rare: it can be exercised at most once per
slot for the lifetime of the batch, and even though it skips the voting
process, it always clears out whichever bank previously held the slot
before installing the new holder, so the slot is never left double-booked.

The full action set is: Propose(s, v) -- bank v announces its candidacy for
free slot s, opening a fresh voting round; Vote(s, v) -- bank v casts a yes
vote for the current candidacy on slot s; Commit(s) -- once the vote count
for slot s reaches quorum and the slot is still free, it becomes allocated
to the proposer; Release(s, v) -- bank v, which currently holds slot s,
gives it back to the free pool; and AdminOverride(s, v) -- the privileged
admin bypasses voting and force-allocates slot s to bank v, clearing any
prior holder and any in-flight vote, usable at most once per slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No settlement slot is ever held by more than one bank at
the same time, whether it was acquired through a completed quorum vote or
pushed through directly by the admin override.

---- MODULE W4Od17m0p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Bags, Stations, NoBag

VARIABLES version, pendingBag, pendingVer, loaded, crashed

vars == <<version, pendingBag, pendingVer, loaded, crashed>>

\* An airport baggage router uses optimistic locking: a routing station
\* reads a bag's current version, then tries to commit the irreversible
\* physical load of that bag onto its plane only if the version has not
\* moved since its read.  If another station already loaded the bag in
\* the meantime, the version has advanced and the stale station must
\* retry with a fresh read instead of double-loading the bag.  Exactly one
\* station may crash silently while holding a stale read; because the
\* locking is optimistic (no station ever blocks another), the surviving
\* stations keep routing bags regardless.

Init ==
  /\ version = [b \in Bags |-> 0]
  /\ pendingBag = [k \in Stations |-> NoBag]
  /\ pendingVer = [k \in Stations |-> 0]
  /\ loaded = {}
  /\ crashed = {}

ReadVersion(k, b) ==
  /\ k \notin crashed
  /\ pendingBag[k] = NoBag
  /\ b \notin loaded
  /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![k] = b]
  /\ pendingVer' = [pendingVer EXCEPT ![k] = version[b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, loaded, crashed>>

CommitLoad(k) ==
  /\ k \notin crashed
  /\ pendingBag[k] # NoBag
  /\ pendingVer[k] = version[pendingBag[k]]
  /\ pendingBag[k] \notin loaded
  /\ loaded' = loaded \cup {pendingBag[k]}
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![pendingBag[k]] = version[pendingBag[k]] + 1]
  /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![k] = NoBag]
  /\ pendingVer' = [pendingVer EXCEPT ![k] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

RetryConflict(k) ==
  /\ k \notin crashed
  /\ pendingBag[k] # NoBag
  /\ pendingVer[k] # version[pendingBag[k]]
  /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![k] = NoBag]
  /\ pendingVer' = [pendingVer EXCEPT ![k] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, loaded, crashed>>

Crash(k) ==
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ crashed' = {k}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, pendingBag, pendingVer, loaded>>

Recover(k) ==
  /\ k \in crashed
  /\ pendingBag[k] # NoBag
  /\ pendingBag' = [pendingBag EXCEPT ![k] = NoBag]
  /\ pendingVer' = [pendingVer EXCEPT ![k] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, loaded, crashed>>

ReadVersionK(k) == \E b \in Bags : ReadVersion(k, b)

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in Stations : ReadVersionK(k) \/ CommitLoad(k) \/ RetryConflict(k) \/ Crash(k) \/ Recover(k)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A k \in Stations : WF_vars(ReadVersionK(k)) /\ SF_vars(CommitLoad(k)) /\ WF_vars(RetryConflict(k))

\* Any station still holding a read on a bag that someone else already
\* loaded necessarily holds a stale (strictly smaller) version number, so
\* its optimistic commit guard can never pass -- the bag cannot be loaded
\* a second time.
BagLoadFencing ==
  \A k \in Stations :
    (pendingBag[k] # NoBag /\ pendingBag[k] \in loaded) =>
      pendingVer[k] < version[pendingBag[k]]

AllBagsEventuallyLoaded == <>(loaded = Bags)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Bags = {b1, b2, b3}
  Stations = {k1, k2}
  NoBag = NoBag
INVARIANT BagLoadFencing
PROPERTY AllBagsEventuallyLoaded
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An airport baggage router directs suitcases from check-in belts onto the
correct outbound flight using optimistic locking with retry instead of a
central lock manager. Each bag carries a version counter. A routing station
that wants to load a bag onto its plane first reads the bag's current
version, then later attempts to commit the load -- but the commit only
succeeds if the bag's version has not changed since the station read it.
Loading a bag onto a plane is the irreversible action in this system: once
it happens the bag's version is bumped forward, and it must happen exactly
once per bag. If two stations race for the same bag, whichever commits
first bumps the version and wins; the other station's commit attempt now
sees a mismatched version, so it must throw away its stale read and retry
with a fresh one rather than risk double-loading the bag.

Router hardware at one station can freeze up without warning while it is
still holding a stale read on some bag. The model allows exactly one
station to crash silently. Because the locking here is optimistic --
no station ever holds an exclusive lock that could block another --
the crash of one station never prevents the surviving stations from
independently reading and loading the same bags; a background monitor
eventually clears the crashed station's stale pending read so its record
does not linger indefinitely.

The full action set is: ReadVersion(k, b) -- station k, not crashed and
currently idle, reads bag b's current version and remembers it as its
pending attempt; CommitLoad(k) -- station k's pending bag is loaded onto
the plane, and the bag's version is bumped, but only if the version k
remembered still matches the bag's current version; RetryConflict(k) --
station k discovers its remembered version is now stale (someone else
already committed) and discards the pending attempt so it can re-read
fresh; Crash(k) -- station k silently fails, possibly while still holding
a pending read (allowed for at most one station in the whole run); and
Recover(k) -- a monitor clears a crashed station's stale pending read.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any station still holding a read on a bag that has already
been loaded necessarily holds a version number strictly older than the
bag's current version, so that station's optimistic commit can never
succeed and no bag is ever loaded twice.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bag is eventually loaded onto its plane, even
though up to one routing station may crash silently while holding a stale
read on some bag.

---- MODULE W4Od13m4p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Messages, Capacity

VARIABLES inFlight, queue, processed, resent

vars == <<inFlight, queue, processed, resent>>

\* A network of vending machines reports stock levels to a central hub
\* over an unreliable link that can reorder messages -- `inFlight` is
\* modeled as a set rather than a sequence so any pending report may be
\* delivered next, regardless of send order. The hub only pulls a report
\* out of the network into its bounded ingest queue when there is spare
\* room (backpressure keyed on Capacity). Because reordering can delay a
\* report's acknowledgement, a machine may resend a report it fears was
\* lost, even after the original has already been queued or processed --
\* the invariant checks that this duplication can never push the hub's
\* queue past its bound.

Init ==
  /\ inFlight = {}
  /\ queue = {}
  /\ processed = {}
  /\ resent = {}

Send(m) ==
  /\ m \notin inFlight
  /\ m \notin queue
  /\ m \notin processed
  /\ inFlight' = inFlight \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, processed, resent>>

Admit(m) ==
  /\ m \in inFlight
  /\ Cardinality(queue) < Capacity
  /\ queue' = queue \cup {m}
  /\ inFlight' = inFlight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<processed, resent>>

Process(m) ==
  /\ m \in queue
  /\ processed' = processed \cup {m}
  /\ queue' = queue \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inFlight, resent>>

\* Reordering can delay a report's delivery long enough that the sending
\* machine gives up waiting and resends a duplicate -- even if the
\* original copy is already sitting in the queue or already processed.
Resend(m) ==
  /\ m \in (inFlight \cup queue \cup processed)
  /\ m \notin resent
  /\ inFlight' = inFlight \cup {m}
  /\ resent' = resent \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, processed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Messages : Send(m) \/ Admit(m) \/ Process(m) \/ Resend(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The hub's bounded ingest queue never holds more reports than its
\* configured Capacity, no matter how many duplicate resends the flaky,
\* reordering network produces.
CapacityBound == Cardinality(queue) <= Capacity

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Messages = {m1, m2, m3, m4}
  Capacity = 2
INVARIANT CapacityBound
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A regional vending machine network has dozens of machines reporting stock
levels back to a central hub over a cheap, unreliable radio link. The link
can reorder messages in transit -- a report sent later can arrive before
one sent earlier -- so the model treats the set of in-flight reports as an
unordered pool rather than an ordered channel: any pending report can be
the next one the hub sees. The hub protects itself with a bounded work
queue: it will only pull a report out of the network and admit it into its
local processing queue when the queue has spare room under its configured
Capacity. This backpressure is what keeps a burst of simultaneous machine
reports from overwhelming the hub's processing pipeline.

Because reordering can delay how quickly a machine sees an acknowledgement
for its report, a machine may conclude (incorrectly) that its report was
lost and resend a duplicate copy -- even if the original has already been
admitted into the queue or fully processed by the hub. The concern this
model checks is purely about capacity: no matter how many duplicate resends
the flaky, reordering network produces, the hub's bounded queue must never
hold more reports than its configured Capacity allows.

The full action set is: Send(m) -- a vending machine transmits a fresh
stock report m into the network's in-flight pool; Admit(m) -- the hub pulls
report m out of the in-flight pool into its bounded processing queue,
guarded by spare capacity; Process(m) -- the hub finishes handling a queued
report, removing it from the queue; and Resend(m) -- a machine, having
given up waiting for an acknowledgement because of network reordering,
retransmits report m into the in-flight pool even if the original copy is
already queued or already processed, capped at one resend per report.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The hub's ingest queue never holds more reports at once
than its configured Capacity, regardless of how the reordering network
delays deliveries or how many duplicate resends occur.

---- MODULE W4Od6m2p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants, NoCoord

VARIABLES coordinator, epoch, carStatus, commitEpoch, crashed

vars == <<coordinator, epoch, carStatus, commitEpoch, crashed>>

\* An elevator bank dispatches a single car move by running two-phase
\* commit across that car's own participant subsystems (motor controller,
\* door interlock, safety brake): a dispatch coordinator is elected under
\* a monotonic epoch, each subsystem votes once prepared, and only once
\* every live subsystem has voted does the coordinator commit, stamping
\* the round with the current epoch.  A subsystem may only execute its
\* part of the move while that stamped epoch still matches the live
\* epoch -- if a coordinator failover bumped the epoch in the meantime,
\* the old commit is stale and no subsystem may act on it.  Exactly one
\* participant (coordinator or subsystem) may crash silently.

Init ==
  /\ coordinator = NoCoord
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ carStatus = [c \in Participants |-> "none"]
  /\ commitEpoch = 0
  /\ crashed = {}

Elect(n) ==
  /\ coordinator = NoCoord
  /\ n \notin crashed
  /\ coordinator' = n
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ carStatus' = [c \in Participants |-> "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<commitEpoch, crashed>>

Crash(n) ==
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ crashed' = {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coordinator, epoch, carStatus, commitEpoch>>

DetectFailure ==
  /\ coordinator # NoCoord
  /\ coordinator \in crashed
  /\ coordinator' = NoCoord
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, carStatus, commitEpoch, crashed>>

Vote(c) ==
  /\ coordinator # NoCoord
  /\ coordinator \notin crashed
  /\ c \notin crashed
  /\ carStatus[c] = "none"
  /\ carStatus' = [carStatus EXCEPT ![c] = "yes"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coordinator, epoch, commitEpoch, crashed>>

Commit ==
  /\ coordinator # NoCoord
  /\ coordinator \notin crashed
  /\ commitEpoch # epoch
  /\ \A c \in Participants \ crashed : carStatus[c] = "yes"
  /\ commitEpoch' = epoch
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coordinator, epoch, carStatus, crashed>>

\* A subsystem executes its share of the physical move only while the
\* commit it is acting on still matches the current epoch -- this is the
\* fencing check that keeps a stale or superseded commit from authorizing
\* any further action.
Move(c) ==
  /\ commitEpoch = epoch
  /\ c \notin crashed
  /\ carStatus[c] = "yes"
  /\ carStatus' = [carStatus EXCEPT ![c] = "moved"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coordinator, epoch, commitEpoch, crashed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Participants : Elect(n) \/ Crash(n)
  \/ DetectFailure
  \/ \E c \in Participants : Vote(c) \/ Move(c)
  \/ Commit

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A n \in Participants : WF_vars(Elect(n))
  /\ WF_vars(DetectFailure)
  /\ \A c \in Participants : WF_vars(Vote(c)) /\ WF_vars(Move(c))
  /\ WF_vars(Commit)

\* A subsystem that has executed its move can only have done so under a
\* commit that is still current -- an epoch change since the commit (a
\* coordinator failover) must retroactively be impossible to observe
\* alongside a "moved" status, since Elect always clears carStatus first.
NoStaleAuthorization ==
  \A c \in Participants : carStatus[c] = "moved" => commitEpoch = epoch

AllLiveParticipantsEventuallyAct ==
  <>(\A c \in Participants : c \notin crashed => carStatus[c] = "moved")

  Participants = {p1, p2}
  NoCoord = NoCoord

PROPERTY AllLiveParticipantsEventuallyAct

nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank dispatches a car to answer a floor call by
running two-phase commit across that car's own participant subsystems --
the motor controller, the door interlock, and the safety brake are each
modeled as a participant that must agree before the car actually moves. A
dispatch coordinator is elected among the subsystems under a monotonic
epoch counter; each time a new coordinator takes over, the epoch increases
and any previous round's votes are wiped. While a coordinator is active,
every live subsystem prepares and votes, and only once every live subsystem
has voted does the coordinator commit the round, stamping it with the
epoch that was current at commit time.

A subsystem is only allowed to carry out its share of the physical move
while the commit it is acting on still matches the bank's current epoch.
If the coordinator fails over in between -- because the old coordinator
crashed and a new one took its place under a fresh epoch -- the old commit
becomes stale, and no subsystem may act on it: since a coordinator failover
always wipes every subsystem's vote before the new round starts, a stale
commit can never coexist with a subsystem that has actually finished its
move. The bank tolerates exactly one silent crash among the coordinator and
subsystems combined; a background watchdog notices when the coordinator
itself has crashed and clears the role so a fresh election can happen.

The full action set is: Elect(n) -- subsystem n becomes the new dispatch
coordinator whenever the role is vacant and n has not crashed, starting a
fresh, higher epoch and clearing every subsystem's vote; Crash(n) --
subsystem n silently fails, whether it is the coordinator or an ordinary
participant (allowed for at most one subsystem in the whole run);
DetectFailure -- the watchdog notices the coordinator has crashed and
vacates the role; Vote(c) -- a live subsystem c, while a live coordinator
is active, casts its prepare vote; Commit -- once every live subsystem has
voted, the coordinator commits the round and stamps it with the current
epoch; and Move(c) -- a live subsystem c executes its share of the
physical move, but only while the commit's stamped epoch still matches the
bank's current epoch.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A subsystem that has executed its move can only have done
so under a commit whose stamped epoch still matches the bank's current
epoch -- no subsystem ever acts on a stale commit left behind by a
superseded, failed-over coordinator.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every subsystem that never crashes eventually executes
its share of the elevator move, even though up to one participant --
coordinator or ordinary subsystem -- may crash silently during the round.

---- MODULE W4Od7m0p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Containers

VARIABLES yardSet, stagingSet, shipSet, version, pending

vars == <<yardSet, stagingSet, shipSet, version, pending>>

\* A container-ship crane yard moves each container Yard -> Staging -> Ship
\* using optimistic locking: a move command is stamped with the version
\* the crane control system read when it issued the command, and the
\* command sits in an unordered pending pool -- modeled as a set rather
\* than a sequence -- so commands for the same or different containers can
\* be delivered and applied in any order.  A command only actually moves a
\* container if its stamped version still matches the container's current
\* version; a stale command (superseded by a reordered, already-applied
\* command) is simply discarded and the crane must retry with a fresh
\* read.  The invariant checks that every container is always accounted
\* for in exactly one yard stage -- nothing is ever created or destroyed
\* by a stale application or a lost retry.

Commands == [c : Containers, target : {"Staging", "Ship"}, expVer : 0..2]

Init ==
  /\ yardSet = Containers
  /\ stagingSet = {}
  /\ shipSet = {}
  /\ version = [c \in Containers |-> 0]
  /\ pending = {}

IssueMove(c) ==
  /\ c \notin shipSet
  /\ LET target == IF c \in yardSet THEN "Staging" ELSE "Ship"
         cmd == [c |-> c, target |-> target, expVer |-> version[c]]
     IN /\ pending' = pending \cup {cmd}
        /\ UNCHANGED <<yardSet, stagingSet, shipSet, version>>

ApplyMove(cmd) ==
  /\ cmd \in pending
  /\ cmd.expVer = version[cmd.c]
  /\ pending' = pending \ {cmd}
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![cmd.c] = version[cmd.c] + 1]
  /\ IF cmd.target = "Staging"
     THEN /\ yardSet' = yardSet \ {cmd.c}
          /\ stagingSet' = stagingSet \cup {cmd.c}
          /\ shipSet' = shipSet
     ELSE /\ stagingSet' = stagingSet \ {cmd.c}
          /\ shipSet' = shipSet \cup {cmd.c}
          /\ yardSet' = yardSet

DiscardStale(cmd) ==
  /\ cmd \in pending
  /\ cmd.expVer # version[cmd.c]
  /\ pending' = pending \ {cmd}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardSet, stagingSet, shipSet, version>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Containers : IssueMove(c)
  \/ \E cmd \in Commands : ApplyMove(cmd) \/ DiscardStale(cmd)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every container is always in exactly one yard stage -- the three stage
\* sets partition Containers at every reachable state, so reordered move
\* commands and stale-version retries can never conjure a duplicate
\* container or lose one entirely.
Conservation ==
  /\ yardSet \cup stagingSet \cup shipSet = Containers
  /\ yardSet \cap stagingSet = {}
  /\ yardSet \cap shipSet = {}
  /\ stagingSet \cap shipSet = {}

  Containers = {c1, c2, c3}
INVARIANT Conservation

nl:
A container-ship crane yard moves every container through three stages on
its way to departure: it starts in the Yard, gets relocated to a Staging
lane, and finally gets hoisted into the Ship's hold. Rather than locking a
container while a crane works on it, the yard's control system uses
optimistic locking with retry: whenever a crane wants to advance a
container to its next stage, it issues a move command stamped with the
version number it last read for that container. That command does not
travel over a reliable, ordered channel -- the yard's wireless dispatch
network can reorder commands in transit, so commands for the same or
different containers may be delivered and applied in any order, not
necessarily the order they were issued.

When a move command is finally applied, the control system first checks
whether its stamped version still matches the container's current version.
If it does, the container safely advances to the command's target stage
and its version is bumped. If it does not -- because a reordered, more
recent command for that same container already applied and moved the
version forward -- the stale command is simply discarded, and the crane
that issued it must read the container's fresh state and retry with a new
command. The concern this model checks is conservation: no matter how
badly the network reorders commands or how many stale retries occur, every
container must always be accounted for in exactly one of the three yard
stages -- never appearing in two stages at once, and never disappearing
from all three.

The full action set is: IssueMove(c) -- a crane issues a move command for
container c, stamped with c's current version and targeting c's next
stage; ApplyMove(cmd) -- a pending move command is applied, advancing its
container to the target stage and bumping its version, but only if the
command's stamped version still matches the container's current version;
and DiscardStale(cmd) -- a pending move command whose stamped version no
longer matches the container's current version is thrown away as stale,
forcing the issuing crane to retry with fresh state.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every container is always in exactly one of the Yard,
Staging, or Ship stages -- the reordering network and its stale-version
retries can never cause a container to be counted in two stages
simultaneously or to vanish from all three.
